नर्य: नर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. manly, human, (often with अपस्, a manly deed, a heroic deed); strong, powerful; suitable or agreeable to men (as food); (अस्), m. a man, a person; an epithet of Indra; of Agni Gārhapatya; N. of a man; (आ), m. du., scil. उभा शंसा, the two objects of desire, i. e. heaven and earth [cf. नराशंस]; (आस्), m. pl. epithet of the Maruts; (अम्), n. a manly act, manly deed; a gift for men. —नर्यापस् (°य-अप्°), आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. performing manly deeds; (Sāy.) performing deeds agreeable or suitable to men.
नरक: नरक नरक, अस्, अम्, m. n. (said to be fr. rt. नॄ), hell, the place of torment (distinguished fr. पाताल, the lower regions, q. v.), including a num-ber of places of torture of various descriptions, gene-rally said to be twenty-one in number [cf. नारक]; (Hell is sometimes personified as a son of Anṛta and Nirṛti or Nikṛti); (अस्), m., N. of a demon, a son of Bhūmi or Earth (therefore called Bhauma, haunting Prāg-jyotiṣa and slain there by Kṛṣṇa); N. of a man; N. of a district; of a place of pilgrimage. —न-रक-कुण्ड, अम्, n. a pit or abyss in hell wherein the wicked are tormented, (eighty-six such are enume-rated). —नरक-जित्, त्, m. ‘vanquisher of the demon Naraka,’ epithet of Viṣṇu-Kṛṣṇa. —नरक-दे-वता, f. ‘the deity of hell,’ Nirṛti; Misfortune per-sonified as a goddess. —नरक-भूमि, इस्, f. a division of hell, (of which seven are enumerated.) —नरक-रूपिन्, ई, इणी, इ, ‘hell-formed,’ hellish. —नरक-वर्ग, अस्, m. ‘the hell chapter,’ N. of a chapter of Amara-siṃha's Nāma-liṅgānuśāsana. —नरक-वर्णन, अम्, n. ‘description of hell,’ N. of a chapter of the Revā-māhātmya. —नरक-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, living or being in hell; (आ), f. the river of hell, Vaitaraṇī. —नरक-स्वर्ग-प्राप्ति-प्रकार-वर्णन, अम्, n. ‘description of the mode of obtaining heaven and hell,’ N. of the eighth chapter of the Māgha-māhātmya. —नरकान्तक (°क-अन्°), अस्, m. ‘destroyer of the demon Naraka,’ an epithet of Kṛṣṇa-Viṣṇu. —नरकामय (°क-आम्°), अस्, m. the soul after death; a ghost or spirit. —नरकारि (°क-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy of the demon Naraka,’ an epithet of Kṛṣṇa-Viṣṇu. —नरकावास (°क-आव्°), अस्, m. ‘one whose abode is hell,’ an inhabitant of hell. —नरकौकस् (°क-ओक्°), आस्, m. an inhabitant of hell.
नरकाय: नरकाय, Nom. A. नरकायते, &c., to repre-sent a hell; to resemble or be similar to hell.
नरङ्ग: नरङ्ग नरङ्ग, अस्, m. pimples on the face (= वरण्डक); (अम्), n. the penis; (wrong form for नराङ्ग, see col. 1.)
नरद: नरद नरद, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), a par-ticular substance or article of commerce, a kind of perfume ? [cf. नलद]; (अस्), m., N. of a Brāhman.
नरदिक: नरदिक, अस्, ई, अम्, dealing in the substance called Narada.
नरिष्टा: नरिष्टा नरिष्टा, f., Ved. joking, chatter-ing; sport, pastime; [cf. नर्म, नर्मन्।]
नरिष्यत्: नरिष्यत् न-रिष्यत्, अन्, m., N. of a son of Manu Vaivasvata.
नरिष्यन्त: नरिष्यन्त, अस्, m., N. of a son of Marutta.
नरीय: नरीय नरीय, अस्, m., N. of a son of Bhaṅga-kāra; (also read नारेय।)
नरुण: नरुण नरुण, अस्, m. (fr. rt. नॄ), Ved. (according to a commentator) a leader.
नर्कुटक: नर्कुटक नर्कुटक, अम्, n. a nose [cf. न-कुट]; a kind of metre consisting of four lines of seventeen syllables each; [cf. नर्दटक।]
नर्त: नर्त नर्त, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. नृत्, the initial न् of which is not liable to become ण्), dancing; (अस्), m. dancing, dance.
नर्तक: नर्तक, अस्, m. a dancer, a player of any de-scription; an actor, gesticulator, mime, mummer; a bard, herald; an elephant; a peacock; a species of reed [cf. पोटगल]; (ई), f. a female dancer, actress, singing girl; a female elephant; a peahen; a kind of perfume (= नलिका; cf. नटी); (अस्, आ, अम्, fr. the Caus.), causing to dance; (अस्), m. a dancing-master.
नर्तक; add — अम्, n. a kind of mythical weapon.
नर्तन: नर्तन, अस्, m. a dancer; (अम्), n. the act of dancing, gesticulating, acting, performing on the stage; [cf. नर्तना-गृह।] —नर्तन-प्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, fond of dancing; (अस्), m. a peacock. —नर्-तन-शाला, f. or नर्तनागार (°न-अग्° or -आग्°), अम्, n. or नर्तना-गृह, अम्, n. a dancing-room. —नरतन-स्थान, अम्, n. a dancing-place.
नर्तयितृ: नर्तयितृ, ता, m. ‘one who causes to dance,’ a dancing-master.
नर्तित: नर्तित, अस्, आ, अम्, danced; made to dance; dandled; dancing.
नर्तिन्: नर्तिन्, ई, इनी, इ, dancing; [cf. वंश-न्°।]
नर्तू: नर्तू, ऊस्, f. a female dancer or actress.
नर्द्: नर्द् नर्द् (connected with rt. नद्), cl. 1. P. (ep. also A.) नर्दति (-ते), ननर्द, नर्दिता, नर्दिष्यति, अनर्दीत्, नर्दितुम्, to bellow, roar, shriek, sound; to go, move; [cf. pro-bably Hib. nuail-im, ‘I roar, howl;’ nuail, ‘roar-ing, howling.’]
नर्द: नर्द, अस्, आ, अम्, bellowing, roaring, sounding; [cf. गो-न्°।]
नर्दत्: नर्दत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, roaring, sounding; praising aloud; proclaiming.
नर्दन: नर्दन, अस्, m. ‘one who roars,’ N. of a Nāga-rāja; (अम्), n. sounding, roaring, making a noise; celebrating, praising aloud.
नर्दनीय: नर्दनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be sounded; to be celebrated or praised aloud.
नर्दमान: नर्दमान, अस्, आ, अम्, shouting, roaring.
नर्दित: नर्दित, अस्, आ, अम्, roared, sounded, bellowed; celebrated, loudly praised; (अम्), n. sound, roar, bellow, bellowing; (अस्), m. a kind of die or a throw at dice, the chief die, (commonly नादी or नान्दी, perhaps ‘an ace,’ cf. वृष, a N. for the chief die in Nala VII. 6.)
नर्दिन्: नर्दिन्, ई, इनी, इ, sounding, roaring, making a noise; [cf. गेहे-न्°।]
नर्दटक: नर्दटक नर्दटक, अम्, n. a kind of metre consisting of four lines of seventeen syllables each; (wrongly written नर्धटक; cf. नर्कुटक।)
नर्दबुद: नर्दबुद नर्दबुद or नर्दवुद, अस्, m., Ved. an epithet of Indra.
नर्धटक: नर्धटक नर्धटक, wrong form for नर्-दटक।
नर्ब्: नर्ब् नर्ब्, cl. 1. P. नर्बति, &c., to go, move; [cf. rt. नम्ब्।]
नर्म: नर्म नर्म, अस्, m., Ved. sport, pastime; [cf. नरिष्टा।]
नर्मठ: नर्मठ, अस्, m. a jester; a rake, lecher, liber-tine; sport, amusement; coition; the nipple; the chin.
नर्मन्: नर्मन्, अ, n. sport, play, amusement, pastime; diversion; jest, joke, (नर्माणि कृ, to joke); wit, humour; (अणा), ind. in jest, by way of jest. —नर्-म-कील, अस्, m. a husband. —नर्म-गर्भ, अस्, m. a secret lover. —नर्म-द, अस्, आ, अम्, delight-ing, making happy, giving or causing pleasure; (अस्), m. a jester; the associate or companion of a person's sports or amusements; N. of the son of Lāḍana; (आ), f. the Narma-dā or modern Nerbudda river, which, rising in the Vindhya mountains, runs west-ward to the gulf of Cambay, (personified as the wife of Puru-kutsa and mother of Trasa-dasyu); a sister of the Uragas or serpents; a daughter of the Soma-pas; a species of plant (see पृक्का). —नर्मदा-तट-देश, अस्, m., N. of a district mentioned in the Ratna-koṣa. —नर्मदा-तीर-गमन, अम्, n., N. of the seventeenth chapter of the Uttara-kāṇḍa of the Rāmāyaṇa. —नर्मदा-तीर्थ, अम्, n. a sacred bathing-place on the Narma-dā; [cf. नार्मद।] —नर्मदा-माहात्म्य, अम्, n. ‘the glory of Narma-dā,’ N. of the 173rd-181st chapter of the Matsya-Purāṇa. —नर्मदेश्वर (°दा-ईश्°), अस्, m. a form of Śiva. —नर्मदेश्वर-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of several sacred bathing-places. —नर्-मदेश्वर-माहात्म्य, अम्, n. ‘the glory of Śiva,’ N. of a chapter of the Śiva-Purāṇa. —नर्मदेश्व-र-लिङ्ग, अम्, n., N. of the ninety-second chapter of the Skanda-Purāṇa. —नर्म-द्युति, इस्, इस्, इ, bright with joy, cheerful, happy, merry; (इस्), f. enjoyment of a joke or any amusement. —नर्म-वती, f., N. of a comedy. —नर्म-सचिव, अस्, m. ‘amusement-companion,’ an associate or promoter of the amusements of a prince or man of rank. —नर्-म-साचिव्य, अम्, n. superintendence of a prince's amusements. —नर्म-सुहृद्, त्, m. = नर्म-स-चिव. —नर्म-स्फूर्ज, अस्, m. happiness or amuse-ment ending in alarm (?). —नर्म-स्फोट, अस्, m. slight or inferior amusement (?).
नर्मय: नर्मय, Nom. P. नर्मयति, &c., to make happy or gladden by jests or sports, exhilarate by jesting and wit.
नर्मट: नर्मट नर्मट, अस्, m. a potsherd; the sun.
नर्मरा: नर्मरा नर्मरा, f. a cavity, a valley; a bellows; an old woman past menstruation; a species of plant (= सरला).
नल्: नल् नल्, cl. 1. P. नलति, &c., to smell; to pain (?); to bind (?); cl. 10. P. नाल-यति, &c., to speak or shine; to bind or confine, (the two meanings ‘smelling’ and ‘binding’ have probably arisen from a confusion between गन्धे and बन्धे in the Dhātu-pāṭha.)
नल: नल नल, अस्, m. (for नड, q. v.), a species of reed, Amphidonax Karka, eight to twelve feet high [cf. नड, नाल, देव-नल]; N. of a king of the Niṣadhas or of the country called Niṣadha, son of Vīra-sena and husband of Damayantī and hero of the celebrated tale called Nala and Damayantī; a son of Niṣadha and father of Nabha or Nabhas; a descendant of the latter Nala, son of Su-dhanvan and father of Uktha [cf. नड]; N. of a son of Yadu; N. of a monkey-chief, son of Tvaṣṭṛ or Viśva-karman, who made a bridge for Rāma from the continent to Laṅkā; N. of a Daitya; N. of a medical author; (in astrology) N. of a particular form of constellation in which all the planets or stars are grouped in double mansions; a deified proge-nitor, wrongly written for नल्व; (ई), f. a kind of fragrant substance, a perfume (= नटी); red arsenic, = मनः-सिला, कुनटी; (अम्), n. the blossom of Nelumbium Speciosum (?); smell, odour; [cf. rt. नल्।] —नल-कानन, आस्, m. pl., N. of a people, (this word may perhaps be separated into नलक-आनन; also read नल-कालक, नभ-कानन।) —नल-कील, अस्, m. the knee. —नल-कूबर and नल-कूवर, अस्, m., N. of a son of Kuvera. —नल-चम्पू, ऊस्, f., N. of a work by Tri-vikrama-bhaṭṭa, also called Damayantī-kathā, describing the fortunes of Nala and Damayantī in a highly artificial mixed style, half prose, half verse; [cf. चम्पू।] —नल-द, अम्, आ, n. f. Indian spikenard, Nardostachys Ja-tamansi (= जटामांसी); (अम्), n. the root of Andro-pogon Muricatus (= उशीर); the honey or nectar of a flower; (आ), f., N. of a daughter of Raudrāśva. —नल-पट्टिका, f. a sort of mat made with reeds, a coarse mat. —नल-पुर, अम्, n., N. of a town. —नल-मीन, अस्, m. a species of sprat or (according to some) a shrimp or prawn; (also read तल-मीन।) —नल-सेतु, उस्, m. ‘Nala's bridge,’ the causeway constructed by the monkey Nala, (a name given to the rocks between Ramisseram and Ceylon, com-monly called Adam's bridge.) —नलेश्वर-तीर्थ (°ल-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place. —न-लोत्तम (°ल-उत्°), अस्, m. a species of reed (= देव-नल). —नलोदय (°ल-उद्°), अस्, m. ‘Nala's rise,’ N. of an artificial poem ascribed to Kāli-dāsa and describing the restoration of the fallen Nala to pros-perity and power. —नलोपख्यान (°ल-उप्°), अम्, n. ‘the story of Nala (and Damayantī),’ N. of a celebrated episode of the Mahā-bhārata.
नलक: नलक, अम्, n. a bone (hollow like a reed), any long bone of the body; the tibia; the radius of the arm; (इका), f. a kind of fragrant substance (= नली, commonly पवारी or पन्ठारी); the legu-minous plant Dolichos Lablab; the plant Polianthes Tuberosa; Dæmia Extensa.
नलकिनी: नलकिनी, f. (fr. an unused नलकिन्), the knee-cap or knee-pan; the leg.
नलदिक: नलदिक, अस्, ई, अम्, dealing in Indian spikenard.
नलित: नलित, अस्, m. a species of vegetable, (commonly नालिता।)
नलिन: नलिन, अम्, n. (connected with नल, its stalk being hollow like that of a reed), a lotus flower or water-lily, Nelumbium Speciosum or Nymphæa Ne-lumbo; the indigo plant; water; (ई), f. a lotus, Nelumbium Speciosum, the flexible stalk of the water-lily; an assemblage of the Nelumbium Speciosum or of lotus flowers; a pond in which the lotus grows or may grow, a place abounding in lotuses, (नलिनी is to नलिन as अब्जिनी to अब्ज, पङ्कजिनी to पङ्क-ज, and पद्मिनी to पद्म); the Ganges of heaven or rather an arm of it; a mystical N. of one of the nostrils (= नलिका); a kind of fragrant substance; the fermented and intoxicating juice of the cocoa-nut; N. of the wife of Aja-mīḍha and mother of Nīla; (अस्), m. the Indian crane (as a synonym of पुष्-कर); a species of shrub (= कृष्ण-पाक-फल)। —नलिन-दल, अम्, n. a leaf of the lotus flower; [cf. नलिनी-दल, नव-नलिन-दलाय।] —नलिनी-खण्ड, अम्, n. an assemblage of the Nelumbium Speciosum. —नलिनी-दल, अम्, n. a leaf of the lotus plant; [cf. नलिन-दल।] —नलिनी-नन्दन, अम्, n. ‘the divine garden near the Nalinī (?),’ N. of a garden of Kuvera. —नलिनी-पद्म-कोष, अस्, m., N. of a particular position of the hands in dancing. —नलिनी-रुह, अस्, आ, अम्, what comes forth or has come forth from a Nelumbium Speci-osum; (अस्), m. an epithet of Brahmā; (अम्), n. the fibres of the stalk of Nelumbium Speciosum. —नलिने-शय, अस्, m. (नलिने, loc. sing.), ‘reclin-ing on a lotus,’ an epithet of Viṣṇu.
नलिनीक: नलिनीक at the end of comp. = नलिनी, q. v.
नल्व: नल्व नल्व, अस्, m. a furlong, a measure of distance = 400 or 104 (?) cubits; (wrongly read नल्ल, नल।) —नल्व-वर्त्मग, अस्, आ, अम्, going the distance of a Nalva; (आ), f. a spreading plant; the orange tree (= काकाङ्गी for नारङ्ग?).
नव: नव 1. नव, अस्, आ, अम् (probably connected with the particle 1. नु, q. v., or less probably with नु for prep. अनु, or by some derived fr. rt. 4. नु, to praise), new, fresh, recent, young, modern; (अस्), m. a crow; a species of plant (= रक्त-पुनर्-नवा); N. of a son of Uśīnara and Navā; (आ), f., N. of a wife of Uśīnara and mother of Nava; (अम्), ind. recently, newly, lately, a short time ago, not long since, just, (the crude नव is prefixed to a past pass. part. in this sense, see नव-बद्ध); [for 2. नव see p. 473, col. 1: cf. Zend नव: Gr. νέο-ς, for νέϝο-ς, νεός, νειός, νε-αρό-ς, νε-ᾱν, νεᾱν-ία-ς, νέ-ᾱξ, νε-οσσό-ς, νε-οττ-ία, νε-οχ-μό-ς, νε-βρό-ς, νέ-ατο-ς, νεί-αιρα, νει-ρό-ν: Lat. novu-s, Noviu-s, nov-īciu-s, nov-āli-s, nov-ellu-s, nov-āre, nov-er-ca, nū-nt-iu-s, de-nuo, nū-per: Osk. Nuv-la, Nuceria: Goth. niu-yi-s, ‘new;’ niuyi-tha, ‘newness:’ Angl. Sax. niwe, neow, niwa: Lith. naú-ye-s, ‘new;’ nauyó-ka-s, ‘a novice:’ Slav. nov-ŭ, ‘new:’ Hib. nua, nuadh.] —नव-कारिका, f. a bride, a woman newly married, (probably wrong reading for नव-वरिका); a new Kārikā or comment. —नव-कालिका, f. (fem. of नव-कालक), a young woman, either one recently married or one in whom menstruation has lately commenced. —नव-कृत्, wrongly for नव-गत्. —नव-गत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. first-born (?). —१। न-व-ग्रह, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. see under नवन्), lately caught; [cf. नव-बद्ध।] —नव-च्छात्त्र, अस्, m. a new scholar, a student, novice. —नव-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, recently born, lately produced, new, young (e. g. नव-जः शशी, the new moon or the moon just becoming visible). —नव-जा, आस्, आस्, अम्, Ved. lately produced, new, young. —नव-जात, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. born anew, new-born, fresh, new. —नव-तर, अस्, आ, अम् (compar.), newer, younger, fresher, &c.; [cf. नवीयस्।] —नव-ता, f. or नव-त्व, अम्, n. freshness, novelty. —नव-दल, अम्, n. the fresh leaf of a lotus flower, any young leaf. —नव-द्वीप, अस्, m. ‘the new island,’ N. of a place now called Nuddea, sixty miles from Calcutta, in the district of Burdwan on the right bank of the Bhāgīrathī or great western branch of the Ganges at the point where it is joined by the Jellinghee. —नव-नगर, अम्, n. ‘the new town,’ N. of a town. —नव-नलिन-दलाय (fr. नव-नलिन-दल), Nom. A. नव-नलिन-दलायते, &c., to resemble the leaf of a fresh lotus blossom. —नवनलिनदलायमान, अस्, आ, अम्, resembling the leaf of a fresh lotus flower. —नव-नी, ईस्, f. or नव-नीत, अम्, n. fresh butter. —नवनीतक, अम्, n. clarified butter. —न-वनीत-धेनु, उस्, f. a quantity of butter presented to Brāhmans, see धेनु. —नव-पर्णादि-भक्-षण, अम्, n. ‘eating of new leaves &c.,’ N. of a chapter of the Purāṇa-sarva-sva. —नव-पल्लव, अम्, n. a new shoot, young sprout. —नव-प्रसूता, f. a woman who has lately brought forth (a child). —नव-प्राशन, अस्, m. eating of new rice or new barley. —नव-फलिका, f. a bride, a newly-married woman; a girl in whom menstruation has recently begun. —नव-बद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, lately caught, recently bound. —नव-मल्लिका, f. Arabian jasmine, Jasminum Sambac; (also read नव-मालिका।) —न-व-मालिका, f. many-flowered Nykanthes, Jasminum Sambac (= नव-मल्लिका); N. of a daughter of Dharma-vardhana, king of Śrāvasti. —नव-मालिनी, f. a kind of metre consisting of four lines of twelve syllables each. —नव-मेघ, अस्, m. a new cloud or one just appearing. —नव-यज्ञ, अस्, m. sacrifice or oblation of the first-fruits of the harvest; a daughter-in-law. —नव-वरिका, f. a newly-married woman; [cf. नव-कारिका।] —नव-वस्त्र, अम्, n. new cloth. —नव-वास्त्व, अस्, m., Ved., N. of a man or of an evil spirit. —नव-शशि-भृत्, त्, m. ‘bearing the new moon (on his brow),’ an epithet of Śiva. —नव-शस्य, अम्, n. the first-fruits of the year's harvest, the grain first matured. —नवशस्येष्टि (°य-इष्°), इस्, f. ‘sacrifice of first-fruits,’ a sacrifice performed on eating the first matured rice or grain of the year; a woman recently delivered. —नवाङ्कुर (°व-अङ्°), N. of a work. —नवान्न (°व-अन्°), अम्, n. new rice, new grain, the first-fruits; the grain first ripened, rice or grain recently matured; a cere-mony observed on first eating the new rice, &c. —नवान्न-भक्षण, अम्, n. ‘eating of new grain,’ N. of a chapter of the Purāṇa-sarva-sva. —नवान्न-स्थाली-पाकामन्त्र, आस्, m. pl., N. of a work. —नवान्नेष्टि (°न-इष्°), इस्, f. sacrifice of the first-fruits, see नवशस्येष्टि. —नवाम्बर (°व-अम्°), अम्, n. new and unbleached cloth. —नवाम्बु (°व-अम्°), n. fresh water. —नवार्म (°व-अर्°), अम्, n., N. of a place. —नवाह (°व-अह), अस्, m. a new day, the first day of a fortnight. —नवी-करण, अम्, n. making new, doing anew, renewing. —नवी-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते, -कर्तुम्, to make new, renew, restaurate, revive. —नवी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, done or made anew, renewed, revived. —नवी-भाव, अस्, m. becoming young or new, renovation. —नवी-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, become new, renewed, revived. —नवेतर (°व-इत्°), अस्, आ, अम्, ‘other than new,’ old. —न-वोढा (°व-ऊढा), f. a newly-married woman, a bride. —नवोद्धृत (°व-उद्°), अम्, n. fresh butter; [cf. नव-नीत।]
नव 2. नव, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 4. नु), praise; panegyric, celebration. (For 1. नव see p. 472, col. 2.)
3. नव = नवन्, nine, in त्रि-णव, q. v.
नवक: 1. नवक, अस्, इका, अम्, = 1. नव, col. 2.
2. नवक, अस्, आ, अम्, consisting of 9; (अम्), n. the aggreagate of nine, nine.
नविष्ठ: नविष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. the newest, youngest, last; (अम्), ind. (?), at last.
नवीन: नवीन, अस्, आ, अम्, = 1. नव, new, fresh, recent, modern. —नवीन-चन्द्र, अस्, m. the new moon. —नवीन-मत-विचार, अस्, m. ‘inquiring into new opinions,’ N. of a philosophical work by Hari-rāma. —नवीन-वेदन्तिन्, ई, m. a modern Vedānta philosopher.
नवीयस्: नवीयस् or नव्यस्, आन्, असी, अस् (compar. of 1. नव), Ved. new, fresh, young, recent, who has done anything or shown himself recently; very new; (अस्), ind. recently, lately; (असे or असा), ind. anew.
नव्य: 1. नव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. new, fresh, young; (अस्), m. a species of plant, = रक्त-पुनर्-नवा; [cf. Lith. nauya-s; Goth. niuyi-s.] —नव्य-मत-विचार, अस्, m. = नवीन-मत-विचार. —नव्य-वत्, ind. like new, ever new (?).
2. नव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. to be praised, praise-worthy, laudable, deserving of praise. —नव्य-वर्-धमान, अस्, m., N. of an author.
नव्य 1. and 2. नव्य, See p. 472, col. 3; and col. 1. of this page.
नवन: नवन, अम्, n. the act of praising, laudation.
नविष्टि: नविष्टि, इस्, f., Ved. a song of praise, hymn; (Sāy.) a new sacrifice or oblation, (as if fr. 1. नव।)
नवत: नवत 1. नवत, अस्, m. (for 2. see col. 2), an elephant's painted or variegated housings; woollen cloth; a cover, blanket, wrapper.
2. नवत, अस्, ई, अम्, the 90th; [cf. एक-न्°, चतुर्-ण्°, चतुर्-न्°, त्रि-न्°, द्वा-न्°, द्वि-न्°।]
नवन्: नवन् नवन्, m. f. n. pl. (said to be fr. rt. 4. नु), nine; [cf. Zend navan, ‘nine:’ Gr. ἐννέα, ἔνα-το-ς, ἔννα-το-ς, εἴνατο-ς, ἐννά-κις, ἐνάκις, εἰνάκις, ἐνα-κόσιοι, ἐννα-κόσιοι, ἐνενή-κοντα, ἐννή-κοντα: Lat. novem, nōnu-s, nov-iens, nōnā-ginta, non-genti: Goth. niun, ‘nine;’ niun-da, ‘the ninth:’ Angl. Sax. nigan, ‘nine:’ Old Germ. niun: Mod. Germ. neun: Old Pruss. nevīn-ts, ‘the ninth:’ Slav. devan-tĭ, ‘nine:’ Lith. devyn-i, ‘nine,’ n changed into d as in debes-i-s, ‘a cloud,’ from Sanskrit नभस्; devī1n-ta-s, ‘the ninth:’ Hib. naoi, ‘nine:’ Cambro-Brit. naw, ‘nine.’] —नवकाण्डिका-भा-ष्य, अम्, n. ‘commentary of nine sections,’ N. of a commentary on Kātyāyana's Śrāddha-sūtras by Nīlā-sura. —नव-कृत्वस्, ind., 9 times. —२। नव-ग्रह, आस्, m. pl. the 9 planets, or sun, moon, five planets, and the ascending and descending nodes. —नवग्रह-मन्त्र, आस्, m. pl. ‘hymns or prayers to the 9 planets (?),’ N. of a work. —नवग्रह-शान्ति, इस्, f. propitiation of the 9 planets. —नव-ग्व, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. ninefold, consisting of 9; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a mythological family often associated with that of Aṅgiras and described as sharing in Indra's battles, regulating the worship of the gods, &c.; (अस्), m. one of the family called Nava-gvas; [cf. दश-ग्व, दशग्विन्।] —नवचत्-वारिंश, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. the following), the 49th. —नव-चत्वारिंशत्, त्, f., 49. —नव-तन्तु, उस्, m., N. of a son of Viśvā-mitra. —नवत्रिंश, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. the following), the 39th. —नव-त्रिंशत्, त्, f., 39. —नव-दश, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. the follow-ing), the 19th; consisting of 19. —नव-दशन्, अ, m. f. n. pl., 19. —नव-दीधिति, इस्, m. ‘nine-rayed,’ Mars, the planet or its deified regent; [cf. नवार्चिस्।] —नव-दुर्गा, f. Durgā in her 9 forms (viz. कुमारिका, त्रि-मूर्ति, कल्याणी, रोहिणी, काली, चण्-डिका, शाम्भवी, दुर्गा, भद्रा). —नव-दोला, f. a litter borne by 9 men. —नव-द्वार, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘nine-doored,’ having 9 gates; an epithet of the body, which has 9 apertures or outlets, as the nostrils, ears, mouth, &c.; [cf. नव-मुख।] —न-व-धा, ind. divided into 9 parts, ninefold, in 9 ways, 9 times. —नव-नवति, इस्, f., 99; (in the Veda the number 99 is used for any large number.) —नवनवति-तम, अस्, ई, अम्, the 99th. —नव-पञ्चाश, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. the following), the 59th. —न-व-पञ्चाशत्, त्, f., 59. —नव-पद्, -पात्, -पदी, पत्, Ved. having 9 feet, consisting of 9 feet. —नव-भाग, अस्, m. the 9th part, especially of an asterism or of a lunar mansion; [cf. नवांश।] —नव-मुख, अस्, ई, अम्, having 9 apertures or openings; [cf. नव-द्वार।] —नव-रङ्ग, अम्, n. gift to five and acceptance by four persons of the best Kāyastha families (?). —नवरङ्ग-कुल, अस्, आ, अम्, having the privilege of marrying into 9 distinct families (?). —नव-रत्न, अम्, n., 9 precious gems, viz. a pearl, ruby, topaz, diamond, emerald, lapis lazuli, coral, sapphire, and one called Go-meda, (these 9 jewels are supposed to be related to the 9 planets); the 9 jewels, i. e. the 9 men of letters at the court of Vikramā-ditya were Dhanvantari, Kṣapaṇaka, Amara-siṃha, Śaṅku, Vetāla-bhaṭṭa, Ghaṭa-karpara, Kāli-dāsa, Vara-ruci, and Varāha-mihira; N. of a collection of 9 verses. —नव-रथ, अस्, m., N. of a son of Bhīma-ratha and father of Daśa-ratha. —नव-रात्र, अस्, m. or नवरात्रिक, अम्, n. a period of 9 days; a Soma sacrifice with 9 Sutyā days; 9 days in the middle of the Gavām-ayana; (अम्), n. the period of 9 days from the first of the light half of month Āśvina to the 9th, devoted to the worship of Durgā. —नव-राशिक, the rule of proportion with 9 terms com-prising four proportions. —नवर्च (°व-ऋच), अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. consisting of 9 verses. —नवविंश, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. the following), the 29th. —नव-विंशति, इस्, f., 29. —नव-विध, अस्, आ, अम्, nine-fold, consisting of 9 parts. —नव-व्यूह, अस्, m. an epithet of Viṣṇu; [cf. चतुर्-व्यूह।] —नव-शक्ति, इस्, m. ‘having 9 faculties,’ an epithet of Śiva or Viṣṇu. —नव-शत, अम्, n., 109. —नवशत-तम, अस्, ई, अम्, the 109th. —नव-शस्, ind., 9 by 9, by nines. —नव-शायक, अस्, m. a N. given to any of 9 inferior classes, viz. cowherd, gardener, oilman, weaver, confectioner, water-carrier, potter, blacksmith, and barber. —नव-षट्क, अस्, आ, अम्, consisting of 9 × 6 (strings &c.). —नव-षष्टि, इस्, f., 69. —नवषष्टि-तम, अस्, ई, अम्, the 69th. —न-व-सप्तति, इस्, f., 79. —नवसप्तति-तम, अस्, ई, अम्, the 79th. —नव-सप्तदश, अस्, m., N. of an Atirātra (‘containing 9 Saptadaśa-stotras’). —नव-साहसाङ्क-चरित, अम्, n. ‘the 9 or the new (fr. 1. नव) deeds of king Sāhasāṅka,’ N. of a Campū composed by Śrī-harṣa. —नवांश or नवांशक (°व-आं°), अस्, m. a 9th, a 9th part, especially of an asterism or lunar mansion; [cf. नव-भाग।] —न-वांशक-प, अस्, m. the regent of a Navāṃśaka. —नवांश-नाथ, अस्, m. the regent of a Navāṃśa. —नवाङ्गा (°व-अङ्°), f. a species of plant (= कर्कट-शृङ्गी). —नवायस (°व-आय्°), अम्, n. a medicinal preparation of iron, containing 9 parts of iron. —नवार्चिस् (°व-अर्°), इस्, m. ‘nine-rayed,’ the planet Mars or its deified personification. —नवाशीति (°व-अश्°), इस्, f., 89. —नवाशीति-तम, अस्, ई, अम्, the 89th. —नवाह (°व-अह), अस्, m. a period of 9 days; a Soma sacrifice with 9 Sutyā days; 9 days in the middle of the Gavām-ayana; [cf. नव-रात्र।]
नवति: नवति, इस् (according to lexicographers also न-वती), f., 90. —नवति-तम, अस्, ई, अम्, the 90th. —नवति-धनुस्, उस्, m., N. of an ancestor of Śākya-muni. —नवति-धा, ind. ninetyfold. —न-वति-रथ, अस्, m., N. of an ancestor of Śākya-muni. —नवति-शस्, ind. by nineties, ninety by ninety.
नवतिक: नवतिक, f. (fr. नवति), a paint-brush containing 90 hairs.
नवम: नवम, अस्, ई, अम्, the 9th; (आ), f., scil. तिथि, the 9th day of a lunar half month. —नवमांश (°म-अं°), अस्, m. = नवांश, q. v.
नविन्: नविन्, ई, इनी, इ, consisting of 9, composed of 9.
नवपत्त्रिका: नवपत्त्रिका नव-पत्त्रिका, f. (fr. 1. or 2. नव?), a particular sport described in the Kāma-sūtra by Vātsyāyana.
नविपुला: नविपुला न-विपुला, f. a kind of metre.
नवेदस्: नवेदस् नवेदस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. cognizant, observing, perceiving; appreciating; an observer; ap-preciator (with gen. of the object); [cf. को-विद।]
नश्: नश् 1. नश् (related to rt. नक्ष्; cf. rt. 1. अश्), cl. 1. P. A. नशति, -ते, Aor. आनट् or आनक्, &c. (Pāṇ. VI. 4, 73, but these forms may be referred to rt. 1. अश्), Ved. to reach, attain, obtain; to meet with, find; Caus. नशयति, &c., to cause to obtain or meet with; [cf. Lat. nanciscor.]

नश् 2. नश्, cl. 1. 4. (more usually cl. 4.) P. नशति, नश्यति (ep. also -ते), ननाश (3rd pl. नेशुस्), नशिता, नंष्टा (accord-ing to Vopa-deva also नङ्ग्धा), नशिष्यति, नङ्क्-ष्यति, अनशत्, अनेशत्, नशितुम्, नंष्टुम्, to be lost, disappear, to become invisible, to vanish; to perish, be destroyed, wane; to escape, run away; to come to nothing, be frustrated, be unsuccessful: Caus. नाशयति (ep. also A. नाशयते), -यितुम्, Aor. अनीनशत्, to cause to disappear, make invisible; to cause to perish, suffer to perish, destroy, efface; to violate, deflower; to cause to be lost, to lose; to forget; to extinguish (as a fire); to drive away, cause to fly away; to disappear (in मा व्याघ्रा नीनशुर् वनात्, let not the tigers disappear from the forest, Mahā-bh. Udyoga-p. 862): Desid. निनशिषति, नि-नङ्क्षति: Intens. नानश्यते, नानंष्टि; [cf. Zend naśu, ‘a corpse;’ naś-ista, ‘very destructive:’ Gr. νέκ-υ-ς, νέκυ-ια, νεκ-ρό-ς, probably νόσο-ς, νοῦσο-ς for νοξο-ς, like συν for ξυν: Lat. nex, nec-are, noc-ēre, noxa, per-nicies, ve-ne-nu-m for ve-nec-nu-m: Goth. nau-s, navi-s, ‘a corpse,’ for nag-u-s or nah-u-s.]
3. नश्, क्, क्, क्, or ट्, ट्, ट्, disappearing; perishing; [cf. जीव-न्°।]
नश: 1. नश in दू-णश, दुर्-णश, q. v.; [cf. 1. नाश।]
2. नश, अस्, m. destruction; perishing; [cf. 2. नाश।]
नशन: नशन, अम्, n. disappearing, vanishing; perishing; escaping.
नशितृ: नशितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who disappears; perishing, being lost; destroying, a destroyer; [cf. नंष्टृ।]
नश्यत्: नश्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, perishing, decaying, being destroyed; waning, wasting. —नश्यत्-प्रसूति, इस्, इस्, इ, whose offspring perishes; (इस्), f. a woman who brings forth a dead child. —नश्यत्प्रसूतिका, f. a female bearing a dead child.
नश्वर: नश्वर, अस्, ई, अम्, perishing, perishable; de-structible; transitory, evanescent, subject to decay; destructive, mischievous. —नश्वर-त्व, अम्, n. perishableness, transitoriness; destructiveness.
नष्ट: नष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, lost, disappeared, disappearing; vanished, invisible, lost sight of; perished, destroyed, ruined, spoiled, wasted, annihilated, dead; run away, fled; depraved, debauched; deprived of (at the beginning of a comp.). —नष्ट-चन्द्र, अस्, m., N. of the fourth day in both halves of the month Bhādra. —नष्ट-चेतन, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has lost consciousness, unconscious, fainted, in-sensible, swooning away, losing one's senses. —नष्-ट-चेष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has lost the power of motion; unconscious, fainted, insensible. —नष्-टचेष्ट-ता, f. unconsciousness, insensibility, faint-ing, swooning. —नष्ट-जन्मन्, अ, n. ‘the lost nativity,’ subsequent calculation or casting of a lost nativity. —नष्ट-जातक, अम्, n. = नष्ट-जन्-मन्; N. of the thirteenth Adhyāya in Varāha-mihira's Laghu-jātaka. —नष्ट-दृष्टि, इस्, इस्, इ, one who has lost his sight, blind. —नष्ट-मति, इस्, इस्, इ, one who has lost his intellects. —नष्ट-मार्गण, अम्, n. seeking any lost object. —नष्ट-राज्य, अम्, n., N. of a district to the north-east of Madhya-deśa. —नष्ट-रूप, अस्, आ, अम्, one whose form is lost or no more seen; (आ), f., scil. अनु-ष्टुभ्, a variety of the Anu-ṣṭubh. —नष्ट-विष, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (a snake &c.) that has lost (its) venom. —नष्ट-वीज, अस्, आ, अम्, destitute of the seminal secretion, without the power of pro-creating, impotent. —नष्ट-वेदन, अस्, ई, अम्, finding a lost object. —नष्ट-संस्मृति, इस्, इस्, इ, one who has lost his memory, unmindful, forgetful. —नष्ट-सञ्ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has lost his consciousness. —नष्ट-स्मृति, इस्, इस्, इ, one who has lost his memory, forgetful. —नष्टाग्नि (°ट-अग्°), इस्, m. a Brāhman or householder whose fire has been extinguished or who has lost his conse-crated fire. —नष्टातङ्कम् (°ट-आत्°), ind. without anxiety or fear. —नष्टात्मन् (°ट-आत्°), आ, आ, अ, deprived of mind or sense. —नष्टाप्ति-सूत्र (°ट-आप्°), अम्, n. booty, plunder. —नष्टार्थ (°ट-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, one who has lost his property, reduced to poverty. —नष्टाशङ्क (°ट-आश्°), अस्, आ, अम्, destitute of fear, fearless, dauntless. —नष्टासु (°ट-असु), उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. one whose vital spirits have disappeared. —नष्टेन्दु-कला (°ट-इन्°), f. the day of new moon when it rises invisible. —नष्टेन्-द्रिय (°ट-इन्°), अस्, आ, अम्, one who has lost his organs of sense, deprived of one's senses. —नष्-टैषिन् (°ट-एष्°), ई, इणी, इ, seeking any lost object. —नष्टैष्य, अम्, n. the act of seeking what has been lost.
नष्टि: नष्टि, इस्, f. loss, destruction, ruin.
नशाक: नशाक नशाक, अस्, m. a species of crow.
नस्: नस् 1. नस् (the alternative form for अस्मान् acc. pl., for अस्मभ्यम् dat. pl., and for अस्माकम् gen. pl. of the first personal pronoun अस्मद्, q. v.), us, to us, of us; (नस् is an enclitic and has no accent.)

नस् 2. नस्, cl. 1. A. नसते, नेसे, नसिता, &c., Ved. to approach, to go towards, to join; to copulate (especially as husband and wife); (said to mean also) to be crooked or curved; to bend; to be fraudulent; [cf. Gr. νέ-ο-μαι, νίσ-σ-ο-μαι, νόσ-το-ς, probably also ναίω for νασ-_y_-ω, ἔ-νασ-σα, ἐ-νάσ-θη-ν.]

नस् 3. नस्, f. (probably fr. rt. स्ना, to bathe, or स्नु, to flow, the initial स् being dropped; cf. नौ; नस् is defective in nom. voc. sing. du. and pl., acc. sing. du., but may be optionally substituted for नासिका, q. v., in the acc. pl. and remaining cases, e. g. नसस् or नासिकास्, नसा or नासिकया, नोभ्याम् or नासिकाभ्याम्; only the weak cases नसा, नसि, न-सोस्, however, appear to occur), the nose; [cf. नासा, नासिका; Lat. nasus, naris.] —नः-क्षुद्र, अस्, आ, अम्, small-nosed. —नस्तः-कर्मन्, अ, n. ‘the put-ting into the nose,’ taking snuff. —नस्-तस्, ind. from the nose, into the nose. —नस्य्-ओत, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. नसि loc. sing. + ओत), led by a string through the septum of the nose, fastened by the nose, furnished with a nose-ring; an ox or other animal led by a string through the septum of the nose. —नस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having a nose.
नस: नस (at the end of an adj. comp.) = 3. नस्, the nose, see उन्-न्°, उरू-ण्°, कुम्भी-न्°, खर-ण्°, गो-न्°, द्रु-ण्°, &c.; (आ), f. the nose.
नसि: नसि, the nose (?), in कुम्भी-न्°, q. v.
नस्त: नस्त, अस्, m. the nose; (आ), f. a hole bored in the septum of the nose, cf. नस्तक, नस्-तित; (अम्), n. a sternutatory, snuff. —नस्त-करण, अम्, n. a kind of instrument used by the Bhikṣus for injecting the nose. —नस्त-तस्, ind. (perhaps only = नस्-तस् with reduplicated affix तस्), from the nose, out of the nose. —नस्तोत (°त-ओत), अस्, m. an ox led by a string through his nose; (also read नस्य्-ओत; see under 3. नस्।)
नस्तक: नस्तक, अस्, m. a hole bored in the septum or bridge of the nose of cattle for draught.
नस्तित: नस्तित, अस्, आ, अम्, nozzled, having a hole bored in the septum of the nose, an ox or any other draught animal with a string through its nose, (the sort of rein usually employed in India.)
नस्य: नस्य, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging or relating to the nose, nasal, in the nose; (आ), f. the nose; the string through the nose of an animal [cf. नास्य]; (अम्), n. the hairs in the nose; a sternutatory, snuff. —नस्य-विधि, इस्, m. ‘rules about sternutatories,’ N. of the twenty-seventh chapter of the medical work Śārṅgadhara-saṃhitā.
नसंविद्: नसंविद् न-संविद्, त्, f. unconsciousness; forgetfulness.
नसुकर: नसुकर न-सुकर, अस्, आ or ई, अम्, not easy to be done.
नह्: नह् 1. नह्, cl. 4. P. A. नह्यति, -ते, न-नाह, नेहे, नद्धा, नत्स्यति, -ते, अनात्-सीत्, अनद्ध, नद्धुम्, to bind, tie, bind on, bind round, put on, gird round, bind together; A. to put on one's self, dress, put on armour, arm one's self: Caus. नाहयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अनीनहत्, to cause to bind or tie together, to cause to put on: Desid. निनत्सति, -ते: Intens. नानह्यते, नानद्धि; [cf. Gr. νέ-ω, νή-θ-ω, νῆ-μα, νῆ-σι-ς, νῆ-τρο-ν, νέ-ω, Intens. νη-νέ-ω, νη-έ-ω: Lat. ne-o, ne-men, ne-tu-s, nec-t-o, nexu-s: Old Germ. nā-an, nāw-an, nāh-an, ‘to sew;’ nā-dal, ‘needle;’ nah, ‘near:’ Goth. nethla, ‘a needle;’ nēhva, ‘near:’ Angl. Sax. naedl, ‘needle;’ neah, neh-st, nearra: Eng. nigh: Mod. Germ. näh-en, nad-el, nah, nach, ge-nug: Hib. nasgaim, ‘I bind;’ nas, ‘a tie.’]
2. नह्, त्, f., Ved. a bond, tie; [cf. अक्षा-न्°।]
नहन: नहन, अम्, n., Ved. a bolt, a nail or connecting beam in a wall.
नह्यमान: नह्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being bound, tied, or fettered.
नहि: नहि न-हि, ind. for not, surely not, cer-tainly not, by no means, not at all; न-नहि, cer-tainly not; (नहि is sometimes strengthened in the Veda by other particles, e. g. नह्य् अङ्ग, नहि नु, नहि स्म।) —नहि-मात्र, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), a particular high number; [cf. न-मात्र।]
नहुस्: नहुस् नहुस्, उस्, m. a man, one who does not belong to one's own immediate community, a neighbour [cf. नाभि; Mod. Germ. nahe]; (collec-tively) the neighbourhood.
नहुष: नहुष, अस्, m., Ved. = नहुस्, a man; N. of a son of Manu and author of a Ṛg-veda hymn; N. of an ancient king, one of the lunar race, son of Āyus and grandson of Purū-ravas, father of Yayāti, who took possession of Indra's throne in heaven for a time, but was afterwards deposed and changed into a serpent; (according to others) a son of Ambarīṣa, father of Nābhāga; N. of a serpent-demon; N. of a Marut; an epithet of Kṛṣṇa-Viṣṇu; [cf. नघु-ष, नाहुष, नाहुषि।] —नहुष-चरित, अम्, n. ‘the life of Nahuṣa,’ N. of the 112th chapter of the Bhūmi-khaṇḍa of the Padma-Purāṇa. —न-हुषाख्य (°ष-आख्°), अम्, n. the plant Taber-næmontana Coronaria (= तगर-पुष्प). —न-हुषात्मज (°ष-आत्°), अस्, m., N. of a king, the son of Nahuṣa, also called Yayāti.
नहुष्टर: नहुष्टर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. nearer (?), nearer than a neighbour.
नहुष्य: नहुष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. belonging to a de-scendant of Nahus, belonging to a man in general, human; (अस्), m. a man.
ना: ना ना, ind. = न, no, not.
नाक: नाक नाक, अस्, m. (said to be fr. न + अ-क, where there is no unhappiness), heaven, the vault or ceiling of heaven, the upper sky, the firma-ment, sky, atmosphere, ether, paradise, (often in the Veda with दिवो, gen. of 3. दिव्, or with उत्तम or तृतीय; cf. त्रि-नाक, त्रि-दिव: in Vājasaneyi-saṃhitā XVII. 67, the scale upwards is given as follows, 1. पृथिवी, earth; 2. अन्तरीक्ष, atmo-sphere; 3. दिव्, sky; 4. दिवो-नाक, upper sky; 5. स्वर्-ज्योतिस्, heaven of light or sphere of the luminaries); the sun (?) ; N. of a Maudgalya; N. of a mythical weapon of Arjuna; (अस्, आ, अम्), ‘pain-less (?),’ N. of a dynasty. —नाक-चर, अस्, आ, अम्, walking in the sky (as the Pitṛs). —नाक-नाथ, अस्, m. or नाक-नाथक, अस्, m. ‘guardian of the sky,’ an epithet of Indra. —नाक-नायक, अस्, m. ‘chief of the sky,’ an epithet of Indra. —नाकना-यक-पुरोहित, अस्, m. ‘Indra's chief priest,’ an epithet of Bṛhas-pati. —नाक-पाल, अस्, m. guardian or lord of the sky. —नाक-पृष्ठ, अम्, n. ‘sky-ceiling,’ the upper sky, the uppermost heaven. —ना-क-पृष्ठ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being in the highest heaven. —नाक-लोक, अस्, m. the heavenly world. —नाक-वनिता, f. ‘a nymph of heaven,’ an Apsaras. —नाक-सद्, त्, त्, त्, resting in the firmament, in-habiting the sky; (त्), m. an inhabitant of heaven, a deity; (अस्), m. pl., N. of nine Ekāhas; (त्), f., N. of an Iṣṭakā. —नाकापगा (°क-आप्°), f. the river of heaven, the heavenly Gaṅgā. —नाकेश (°क-ईश), अस्, m. ‘the lord of the sky,’ an epithet of Indra. —नाकेश्वर (°क-ईश्°), अस्, m. ‘the lord of heaven,’ a god. —नाकौकस् (°क-ओक्°), आस्, m. ‘whose dwell-ing is the sky,’ an inhabitant of heaven, a god.
नाकिन्: नाकिन्, ई, m. a deity, god (as dwelling in Nāka). —नाकि-नाथ, अस्, m. ‘chief of the gods,’ an epi-thet of Indra.
नाकु: नाकु नाकु, उस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. नम्), an ant-hill or mole-hill, a burrow; a mountain; N. of a Muni or saint. —नाकु-सद्मन्, आ, m. a snake.
नाकुल: नाकुल नाकुल, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. नकुल), re-lating or belonging to an ichneumon, ichneumon-like, similar to an ichneumon; (अस्), m. a patronymic from Nakula [cf. नाकुलि]; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people; (ई), f. the ichneumon plant, a particular plant sup-posed to furnish the ichneumon or mungoose with an antidote when bitten in a conflict with a snake [cf. गन्ध-नाकुली, नकुलेष्टा]; a sort of pepper, Piper Chaba (= चव्य); the root of the Seemul tree (= कुक्कुटी-कन्द) and several other plants, as य-व-तिक्ता, श्वेत-कण्ट-कारी, सर्प-गन्धा. —ना-कुलान्ध्य (°ल-अन्°), अम्, n. ‘ichneumon blindness,’ a kind of weakness of sight.
नाकुलि: नाकुलि, इस्, m. a descendant of Nakula, a patro-nymic of Śatānīka.
नाक्र: नाक्र नाक्र, अस्, m., Ved. an aquatic animal; [cf. नक्र।]
नाक्षत्र: नाक्षत्र नाक्षत्र, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. नक्षत्र), belonging to the constellations or lunar asterisms, starry, sidereal; (अम्), n. a month computed by the moon's passage through the twenty-seven mansions, or one of thirty days of sixty Ghaṭis each.
नाक्षत्रिक: नाक्षत्रिक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or belonging to the lunar asterisms, sidereal; (अस्), m. a month of twenty-seven days, each day being the period of the moon's passage through a lunar asterism; (ई), f. the state or condition to which a person is subjected agreeably to the asterism presiding over his nativity.
नाग: नाग नाग, अस्, m. (perhaps for original स्नाग; Angl. Sax. snaca; Eng. snake; or connected with नग, a mountain, or नग्न, naked; said to be fr. rt. 1. दह् through change of द् into न्), a snake in general, especially the spectacle-snake or cobra capella, Coluber; a Nāga or fabulous serpent-demon so called, having a human face with the tail of a ser-pent, (the race of these beings is said to have sprung from Kadrū, wife of Kaśyapa [or from Su-rasā], in order to people Pātāla, one of the regions below the earth, their city is called Bhoga-vatī); an elephant; a shark (= तन्तु-नाग); a cruel or tyrannical person; (at the end of a comp.) ‘an elephant of a man,’ any great or pre-eminent person; N. of several plants, the small tree with fragrant blossoms, Mesua Roxburghii [cf. नाग-केशर]; Rottlera Tinctoria (= पुन्-नाग); a Cyperus (= मुस्तक); Piper Betel; a poisonous plant (see नाग-स्तोकक); a cloud; a peg or nail projecting from a wall to hang anything upon; one of the five airs of the body, that which is expelled by eructation; N. of the number seven, (probably to be referred to seven mythical serpents, but eight principal Nāgas are mentioned); N. of a Sādhya; of a Buddhist teacher; of a king of Āryāvarta, contemporary of Samudra-gupta; N. of a dynasty consisting of nine or seven princes; N. of several men; N. of a mountain; of a district; (ई), f. a female Nāga; a female elephant; (अम्), n. tin; lead; one of the astronomical periods called Karaṇas, (it is one of those termed ध्रुव, q. v., or invariable, and corresponds to the last half of Amāvāsya or new moon); the effects of that period on anything done or happening during it; (अस्, ई, अम्), formed or consisting of snakes, serpentine, snaky; relating to serpents or serpent-demons; elephantine, belonging to or resembling an elephant; (आ), f., N. of a woman; [cf. क्षिति-न्°।] —नाग-कन्द, अस्, m. a kind of bulbous plant (= हस्ति-कन्द). —नाग-कन्यका, f. a serpent-virgin. —नाग-कर्ण, अस्, m. a kind of Ricinus (= रक्-तैरण्ड, हस्ति-कर्ण). —नाग-किञ्जल्क, अम्, n. the blossom of Mesua Roxburghii. —नाग-कुमार, अस्, m. a prince of the serpent-demons; N. of a class of deities among the Bhavanādhīśas guarding the treasures of Kuvera. —नाग-केश, अस्, m., N. of a minister of king Nageśa. —नाग-केशर or नाग-केसर, अस्, m. a small tree with fragrant blossoms (commonly Nageśar), Mesua Roxburghii or Ferrea; (अम्), n. the blossom of this tree. —नाग-खण्ड, N. of one of the nine divisions of Bhārata-varṣa. —नाग-गन्धा, f. a species of bulbous plant (= नाकुली or सर्प-गन्धा). —नाग-गर्भ, अम्, n. red lead. —नाग-चूड, अस्, m. ‘snake-crested’ or ‘whose top-knot consists of snakes,’ an epithet of Śiva. —नाग-च्छत्त्रा, f. a kind of plant, Tiaridium Indicum. —नाग-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, produced by or born from a Nāga, &c.; (अम्), n. red lead; tin. —नाग-जिह्वा, f. ‘snake-tongue,’ a species of plant, Asclepias Pseudosarsa; (see शारिवा।) —नाग-जिह्विका, f. red arsenic. —नाग-जीवन, अम्, n. tin. —नागजीवन-शत्रु, उस्, m. ‘enemy of tin,’ orpiment. —नाग-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha. —नाग-दत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, given by Nāgas or serpents; (अस्), m., N. of one of the 100 sons of Dhṛta-rāṣṭra; N. of a man related to Śākya-muni; of a king of Āryāvarta, contemporary of Samudra-gupta. —नाग-दन्त, अस्, m. elephant's tusk or ivory, the tooth or tusk of an elephant; a shelf, peg, or bracket projecting from a wall and used to hang things upon; (आ), f., N. of an Apsaras; (ई), f. a species of sun-flower, Helio-tropium Indicum; a harlot. —नागदन्तक, अस्, m. ivory; a wooden peg or bracket projecting from a wall, a shelf; (इका), f. a plant, commonly called Rāma-dūti, Tragia Involucrata. —नाग-दमनी, f. a particular plant (= जम्बू, जाम्बवती, वृक्का)। —नाग-दलोपम (°ल-उप्°), अम्, n. the tree Xylocarpus Granatum. —नाग-दाशक, अस्, m., N. of a prince. —नाग-देण्टिका, f. the betel plant. —नाग-देव, अस्, m., N. of an author. —नाग-द्रु, उस्, m. a species of Euphorbia used in offerings to the snake-goddess Manasā (= समन्त-दुग्ध)। —नाग-द्वीप, अस्, m., N. of a Dvīpa in Jambū-khaṇḍa or Bhārata-varṣa. —नाग-नक्षत्र, अम्, n., N. of the three asterisms forming the Nāga-vīthi (?). —नाग-नाथ, अस्, m. the king of the ser-pents, a serpent-chief; (अम्), n., N. of a Liṅga sacred to Śiva; (also called नागनाथेश-लिङ्ग।) —नाग-नाभ, अस्, m., N. of a man. —नाग-नामक, अम्, n. tin. —नाग-नामन्, आ, m. holy basil (= तुलसी)। —नाग-नायक, अस्, m. the leader or chief of the Nāgas or snakes. —नाग-नासा, f. the trunk or pro-boscis of an elephant. —नागनासोरू (°सा-ऊरू), ऊस्, f. a woman whose thighs taper like the trunk of an elephant; [cf. करभोरू, p. 205, col. 2.] —नाग-निर्यूह, अस्, m. = निर्यूह and नाग-दन्त, a large pin or bracket projecting from a wall like a shelf. —नाग-पञ्चमी, f. a particular festival, the fifth day in the light half of month Śrāvaṇa; the fifth day in the dark half of month Āṣāḍhā. —नाग-पति, इस्, m. a serpent-chief. —नाग-पत्-त्रा, f. = नाग-दमनी. —नाग-पत्त्री, f. a species of plant (= लक्ष्मणा). —नाग-पद, अस्, m. a kind of coitus. —नाग-पर्णी, f. the betel plant. —नाग-पाल, अस्, m., N. of a man; a prince of Sāśikya. —नाग-पाश, अस्, m. a sort of magical noose or lasso used in battle to entangle an enemy; ‘the serpent-noose,’ an epithet of the weapon of Varuṇa, regent of the waters; a kind of coitus. —नाग-पाशक, अस्, m. a kind of coitus. —नाग-पुर, अस्, m. ‘elephant's town,’ ancient Delhi (= गज-पुर, हास्तिन-पुर). —नाग-पुष्प, अस्, m. several plants, = Rottlera Tinctoria (= पुन्-नाग); (fr. rt. 1. ज्ञा, the initial ज् being lost; said to be fr. rt. म्ना), a mark by which anything is known, sign, token (Ved.); form, manner, mode, character, personal character, nature, species (Ved.); name, appellation, (especially a per-sonal name, as opposed to गोत्र, a family name); merely the name (as opposed to the reality); (in grammar) appellative, common name for a class of objects, noun, word (e. g. मेघ-नामन्, [every] noun or word denoting cloud); substance, essence, (in the Mīmāṃsā phil. opposed to गुण, accidental quality); water (according to Naigh. 1. 11); नाम्ना वच् or नाम ग्रह्, to address by name, mention or call upon by name; नाम कृ or नाम दा or नाम धा or नाम्ना कृ or नाम्ना वि-धा, to give a name, to name, call (e. g. सावित्रीति नामास्याश् चक्रुः, they called her name Sāvitrī; लक्ष्मणम् इति नाम कृतवान्, he named him Lakṣmaṇa; तां दुःख-लब्धिकां नाम्ना चकार, he called her Duḥkha-labdhikā). नामन् often occurs at the end of an adj. comp., in which case the fem. is generally नाम्नी (e. g. विष्णु-शर्म-नामा पण्-डितः, a sage named Viṣṇu-śarman; नदी-नाम्नी कन्या, a girl with the name of a river); but the fem. may be also नामा from नामन् and नामा from a base नाम, which is rarely substituted for नामन् at the end of a comp. (नाम, acc. sing. used as an adverb =) namely, by name (e. g. मा-धवो नाम ब्राह्मणः, a Brāhman, Mādhava by name); indeed, certainly, forsooth, really, of course, even, probably, possibly, perhaps, agreed, granted, granting (e. g. अस्तु नाम स धनी मे किञ्चिद् दधाति, granting [which I doubt] that this rich man will offer me something). नाम as an emphatic particle may have some of the above senses, but is often untranslatable by any single equivalent English word. It is frequently placed after interrogative pronouns (e. g. किं नाम, कथं नाम, कदा नाम, को नाम), when it may be translated by ‘then,’ ‘indeed,’ &c.; अपि नाम at the beginning of a sentence = perhaps, probably, would that! oh that! of course; मा नाम = may it not be that, perhaps, but I hope not; ननु नाम, certainly, evidently; after an imperative नाम = I care not, no matter, if you like, &c. According to native lexicographers नाम implies certainty, possibility, anger, reproach, consent, promise, recollection, sur-prise, pretence, &c.; [cf. Zend nāman: Gr. ὄνο-μα(τ), ἀν-ώνυ-μο-ς, νώνυμν-ο-ς, ὀνομαίνω, ὀνο-μάζω: Lat. co-gnō-men, i-gnō-min-ia, nō-men, nōmin-ā-re, nam, quis-nam, quem-nam = Sanskrit कं नाम, nem-pe = Sanskrit नाम अपि: Umbr. nume, nome, dat. sing. nomn-e: Goth. namō, gen. sing. namin-s, namn-yan, ga-namn-yan, ‘to name:’ Mod. Germ. nāmen, nāme: Angl. Sax. nāma, nemn-an: Eng. name: Slav. i-man, ‘name;’ imen-ova-ti, ‘to name:’ Scot. ainm, ‘name:’ Cambro-Brit. env, ‘name.’] —नाम-करण, अस्, m. a nominal affix; (अम्), n. giving a name, naming a child after birth. —नाम-कर्-मन्, अ, n. the ceremony of naming a child after birth. —नाम-ग्रह, अस्, m. or नाम-ग्रहण, अम्, n. or (Ved.) नाम-ग्राह, अस्, m. addressing or mentioning by name. —नाम-ग्राहम्, ind., Ved. by mentioning the name, by naming. —नाम-तस्, ind., see col. 3. —नाम-देव, अस्, m., N. of a man. —नाम-द्वादशी, f. a religious ceremony, wor-shipping Durgā daily under one of her twelve appel-lations (Gaurī, Kālī, Umā, Bhadrā, Durgā, Kānti, Sarasvatī, Maṅgalā, Vaiṣṇavī, Lakṣmī, Śivā, and Nārāyaṇī). —नाम-ध, अस्, or नाम-धा, आस्, m., Ved. one who gives a name, a name-giver. —नाम-धातु, उस्, m. a verbal base derived from a noun, a nominal verb. —नाम-धारक, अस्, आ, अम्, bearing only the name, being anything only by name (e. g. पुरुषो नाम-धारकः, one who is a man only in name). —नाम-धेय, अम्, n. a name, a title, an appellation, (sometimes at the end of a comp., e. g. किन्-न्°, see under किम्; पुन्-न्°, see under पुंस्); the ceremony of giving a name to a child. —नामधेय-करण, अम्, n. giving a name, naming. —नामधेय-तस्, ind. by name. —नाम-नामिक, अस्, m. an epithet of Viṣṇu. —नाम-नि-धान, अम्, n. ‘a collection of nouns,’ N. of a glossary. —नाम-नियत-प्रवेश, अस्, m., N. of a Samādhi. —नाम-निर्देश, अस्, m. pointing out by name. —नाम-पारायण, अम्, n. ‘a complete col-lection of nouns,’ N. of a glossary. —नाम-मात्र, अम्, n. the mere name, a mere name; (अस्, आ, अम्), having only the name; (एण), ind. by the mere name, merely, nominally. —नाममात्रावशेषित (°र-अव्°), अस्, आ, अम्, having only the name left. —नाम-माला, f. a vocabulary, nomenclature; N. of a Prākṛt glossary of synonyms. —नाम-मुद्रा, f. a seal-ring, signet-ring with a name (engraved on it). —नाम-यज्ञ, अस्, m. a sacrifice only in name. —नाम-लिङ्ग, अम्, n. ‘the gender of nouns,’ N. of a work treating thereof. —नामलिङ्गानुशासन (°ग-अन्°), अम्, n. the rules of gender or lessons on the gender of nouns. —नाम-वर्जित, अस्, आ, अम्, desti-tute of name, nameless, stupid. —नाम-वाचक, अस्, इका, अम्, expressing a name; (in grammar) a pro-per name. —नाम-विधि, इस्, m. ‘name-rule,’ N. of the twenty-third chapter of the Jñāna-khaṇḍa of the Śiva-Purāṇa. —नाम-विस्मृति, इस्, f. forgetting the name (of any one). —नाम-शेष, अस्, आ, अम्, hav-ing only the name left, deceased, dead; (अस्), m. name as the only thing left, dying, death; [cf. आलेख्य-शेष, कीर्त्ति-शेष।] —नाम-सङ्कीर्तन, अम्, n. ‘name-glorification,’ N. of the fourteenth chapter of the Jñāna-khaṇḍa of the Śiva-Purāṇa. —नाम-सङ्ग्रह, अस्, m. a collection of words (exclusive of verbs). —नाम-सारोद्धार (°र-उद्°), अस्, m., N. of a commentary on Hema-candra's Abhidhāna-cintā-maṇi. —नामाख्यातिक (°म-आख्°), अस्, आ, अम्, relating to nouns and verbs. —नामाङ्क (°म-अङ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, marked with a name. —नामाङ्क-शोभित (°म-अङ्°), अस्, आ, अम्, adorned with the mark of the name or with name and cipher. —नामादेशम् (°म-आद्°), ind. by announcing one's name. —नामानुशासन (°म-अन्°), अम्, n. ‘the rules about nouns,’ N. of a lexi-cographical work. —नामापराध (°म-अप्°), अस्, m. abusing (a respectable person) by name, calling names. —नामार्थ-निर्णय (°म-अर्°), अस्, m. ‘inquiry into the bases of nouns,’ N. of a chapter of the Vaiyākaraṇa-bhūṣaṇa-sāra by Koṇḍa-bhaṭṭa. —नामावलि (°म-आव्°), इस्, f. a list of names (especially of a god). —नामाष्टमी-विधान (°म-अष्°), अम्, n., N. of the twenty-fourth chap-ter of the Jñāna-khaṇḍa of the Śiva-Purāṇa.

नारायण: नारायण, अस्, m. (fr. नर, q. v.; sometimes de-rived fr. नार + अयन), ‘son of Nara or the original man,’ patronymic of the personfied Puruṣa or first living being, author of the Puruṣa hymn; he is often associated with Nara or the original man, and identified with Brahmā (in Manu I. 9, 11) and with Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa; in Hari-vaṃśa 4601 Urvaśī is described as springing from his thigh; elsewhere he is regarded as a Kāśyapa or Āṅgirasa [cf. महा-न्°, अर्ध-न्°]; chief of the Sādhyas; the eighth of the nine black Vāsu-devas (with Jainas); the Puruṣa hymn, com-posed by Nārāyaṇa (Ṛg-veda X. 90); N. of the second month, reckoning from Mārgaśīrṣa; N. of a son of Ajāmila; of Bhūmi-mitra; of Nara-hari; N. of several men, authors and commentators; a mystical N. of the letter आ; (अस्, ई, अम्), relating or belonging to Nārāyaṇa or Kṛṣṇa, (the warriors in Kṛṣṇa's army are called Nārāyaṇāḥ in Udyoga-parva 147); (with क्षेत्र) a term applied to the ground on the banks of the Ganges for a distance of four Hastas or cubits from the water; (with तैल) a sort of oil to which efficacy is ascribed in medicine; (ई), f. epithet of Lakṣmī, the goddess of prosperity and wife of Viṣṇu; epithet of Durgā; epithet and patronymic of Indra-senā, wife of Mudgala; epithet of the Ganges or of the Gaṇḍakī (?); the plant Aspa-ragus Racemosus. —नारायण-कण्ठ, अस्, m., N. of an author. —नारायण-कल्प, अस्, m., N. of a work. —नारायण-क्षेत्र, अम्, n. four cubits on either side of the Ganges; see above. —नारायण-गीता, f., N. of a work containing the principles of the sect founded by Rāmānanda. —नारायण-गुप्त, अस्, m., N. of a Gupta prince. —नारायण-चक्रवर्तिन्, ई, m., N. of a grammarian. —नारायण-तार, अस्, m., N. of an author; नारद: नारद नारद, अस्, m. (etymology uncer-tain), N. of a Ṛṣi or rather Devarṣi (i. e. Ṛṣi among the gods) regarded in the Veda as a descendant of Kaṇva and author of certain hymns of the Ṛg-veda (VIII. 13, IX. 104, 105), often associated in the later mythology with Parvata, (he appears on the earth, like Mercury, as a messenger from the gods to men or vice versâ, and is reckoned among the ten Prajā-patis as a son of Brahmā (Manu I. 35), from whose forehead he is said to have been produced; in the modern mythology he is a friend of Kṛṣṇa and is regarded as inventor of the Vīṇā or lute; in epic poetry he is occasionally called a Deva-gandharva, ‘divine Gandharva,’ or a Gandharva-rājan, ‘king of the Gandharvas,’ or simply Gandharva); N. of a son of Viśvā-mitra; of an author; of a mountain; (आ), f. a species of sugar-cane, = इक्षु-मूल; (अस्, ई, अम्), relating to Nārada, composed by him, &c. —नारद-पञ्च-रात्र, अम्, n., N. of a work. —नारद-पुराण, अम्, n., N. of a Purāṇa. —नारदपुराण-सूचन, अम्, n., N. of the sixty-fifth chapter of the Vārāha-Purāṇa. —नारद-प्र-करण, अम्, n. ‘Nārada chapter,’ N. of the 129th chapter of the Kṛṣṇa-khaṇḍa or fourth section of the Brahma-vaivarta-Purāṇa. —नारद-वाक्य, अम्, n. ‘speech of Nārada,’ N. of the sixty-seventh chapter of the Uttara-kāṇḍa or seventh section of the Rāmā-yaṇa. —नारद-संहिता, f., N. of a musical work. —नारद-सनत्कुमार-वाद, अस्, m. ‘discourse of Nārada and Sanatkumāra,’ N. of the 103rd chapter of the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the Padma-Purāṇa. —ना-रद-समागम, अस्, m. ‘arrival of Nārada,’ N. of the twenty-first chapter of the Uttara-kāṇḍa of the Rāmāyaṇa. —नारदेश्वर-तीर्थ (°द-ईश्°), अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-place. —नारदोपदेश (°द-उप्°), अस्, m. ‘the advice of Nārada,’ N. of the first chapter of the Krīḍā-khaṇḍa of the Gaṇeśa-Purāṇa.
नारदिन्: नारदिन्, ई, m., N. of a son of Viśvā-mitra.
नारदीय: नारदीय, अस्, आ, अम्, relating to Nārada, com-posed by Nārada, &c.; (अम्), n. (with or without पुराण), N. of a Purāṇa. —नारदीय-महा-स्थान, अम्, n., N. of a place. —नारदीयोपपु-राण (°य-उप्°), अम्, n., N. of an Upa-Purāṇa.
नारदीयक: नारदीयक, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to or proceeding from Nārada; (अम्), n., N. of a Purāṇa.
नारद्वसव: नारद्वसव नारद्वसव (?), अम्, n., N. of a Sāman.
नारसिंह: नारसिंह नारसिंह, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. नर-सिंह), referring or belonging to Viṣṇu in his man-lion Ava-tāra or incarnation; (अस्), m., N. of Viṣṇu; of a man; of a town. —नारसिंह-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra. —नारसिंह-पुराण, अम्, n., N. of a Purāṇa. —नारसिंहोपपुराण (°ह-उप्°), अम्, n., N. of an Upa-Purāṇa.
नाराच: नाराच नाराच, अस्, m. an iron arrow, an arrow in general; a water-elephant (= जलेभ, अम्बु-हस्तिन्); a bad or cloudy day (?); a species of the Dhṛti metre, also called Narāca, consisting of 4 times 8 iambics; (नाराची or नाराचिका), f. a gold-smith's scales, a fine or assay balance.
नाराशंस: नाराशंस नाराशंस, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. नरा-शंस), Ved. laudatory or eulogistic praise of a man or men, (hence a tale or legend which eulogizes a liberal patron is called Nārāśaṃsī or Nārāśaṃsam); sacred to or belonging to Agni-narāśaṃsa, relating to him, containing him, (applied to certain Soma liba-tions, at which Narāśaṃsa's name is mentioned; applied also to the Pitṛs because reference is made to them at these libations.)
नाराशर्य: नाराशर्य नाराशर्य, अस्, m., N. of a man; (also read पाराशर्य।)
नारिकेर: नारिकेर नारिकेर or नारिकेल, अस्, m. or नारिकेलि, इस् and ई, f. the cocoa-nut tree, the cocoa-nut. —नारिकेल-द्वीप, अस्, m., N. of an island.
नारिङ्गकन्द: नारिङ्गकन्द नारिङ्ग-कन्द, अस्, or अम्, m. or n. (?), the yellow carrot; [cf. नारङ्ग-पत्-त्रक।]
नारी: नारी नारी, f. See नार, p. 479, col. 1.
नारीकेल: नारीकेल नारीकेल, अस्, ई, m. f. the cocoa-nut; (ई), f. fermented liquor made from the water or milk of the cocoa-nut.
नारीच: नारीच नारीच, अम्, n. an esculent root (= commonly नालिता), Corchorus Capsularis; [cf. नाडीका।]
नारीतरङ्गक: नारीतरङ्गक नारी-तरङ्गक, अस्, m. a liber-tine, a catamite; [cf. नाडी-तरङ्ग।]
नारुन्तुद: नारुन्तुद नारुन्तुद (न-अर्°), अस्, आ, अम्, not causing wounds, not hurting.
नार्तिक: नार्तिक नार्तिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. नर्त), re-lating to or connected with dancing (?).
नार्पत्य: नार्पत्य नार्पत्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. नृ-पति), kingly, relating to royalty.
नार्मत: नार्मत नार्मत, अस्, m. (fr. नृ-मत्), a patronymic.
नार्मद: नार्मद नार्मद, अस्, m. (fr. नर्म-दा), a metronymic from Narma-dā.
नार्मर: नार्मर नार्मर, अस्, m. (fr. नृ-मर), Ved. ‘man-slayer,’ N. of a demon.
नार्मिण: नार्मिण नार्मिण, अस्, ई, अम् (perhaps fr. नर्मिन् or नर्मिण, which may be a N. derived fr. नर्म or नर्मन्), Ved. (Sāy.) delightful, joy-ful (= नर्म-वत्).
नार्मेध: नार्मेध नार्मेध, अम्, n. (fr. नृ-मेध), Ved., N. of a Sāman.
नार्य: नार्य नार्य, अस्, m. (fr. नर्य), Ved. pro-bably N. of a person.
नार्यङ्ग: नार्यङ्ग नार्यङ्ग, अस्, m. = नारङ्ग, the orange-tree.
नार्यतिक्त: नार्यतिक्त नार्य-तिक्त = अनार्य-तिक्त, Aga-thotes Chirayta (= किरात-तिक्त).
नार्षद: नार्षद नार्षद, अस्, m. (fr. नृ-षद्), Ved. a patronymic of Kaṇva; N. of a demon (?).
नाल: नाल नाल, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. नल), consisting of reeds, made of a reed or reeds; (आ or ई, अम्), f. n. a hollow or tubular stalk, especially the stalk of the lotus [cf. खर-न्°], of a pot-herb, &c.; (अम्), n. any pipe or tube or tubular vessel of the body, the windpipe, urethra, &c.; a handle; = ताल, आल, yellow orpiment; (आ), f., N. of a river; (ई), f. an instrument for perforating an elephant's ear; a piece of metal on which the hours are struck (= घटी); a period of twenty-four minutes; a lotus flower. —नाल-वंश, अस्, m. = नल, a reed.
नालक: नालक for नाल in चारु-नालक, q. v.
नालायित: नालायित, अस्, आ, अम्, (fr. an unused Nom. ना-लाय), representing the handle (of an axe).
नालि: नालि, इस्, f. = नाडी, any tubular vessel of the body.
नालिक: नालिक, अस्, m. a buffalo; (आ), f. a stalk, the stalk of a lotus, a tube, see गन्ध-न्°, कपाल-न्°; a species of pot-herb (= नालिता); a species of plant (= चर्म-कषा); an instrument for piercing an elephant's ear; = नाडी, a period of twenty-four minutes; (अम्), n. a lotus flower [cf. नालीक]; myrrh; a kind of wind instrument, (perhaps) a flute; a peculiar manner of sitting.
नालिनी: नालिनी, f. (fr. an unused form नालिन्, which is de-rived fr. नाल), a mystical N. of one nostril.
नालीक: नालीक, अस्, m. an arrow (= नाराच, but in the epic poetry different from it); a dart, a javelin, a pike; body, limb (?); a lotus; the fibrous stalk of the lotus; (अम्), n. an assemblage of lotus flowers.
नालीकिनी: नालीकिनी, f. (fr. an unused form नालीकिन्, which is derived fr. नालीक), a multitude or assemblage of lotus flowers, a lotus lake.
नालन्द: नालन्द नालन्द, N. of a village near Rāja-gṛha containing a celebrated Buddhist monastery.
नालन्दर: नालन्दर, N. of a Buddhist monastery.
नालिकेर: नालिकेर नालिकेर, अस्, m. the cocoa-nut tree, the cocoa-nut; N. of a district to the south-east of Madhya-deśa.
नालिकेल: नालिकेल, अम्, n. the cocoa-nut; (various reading for नालिकेर।)
नालिजङ्घ: नालिजङ्घ नालि-जङ्घ, अस्, m. a raven or the carrion-crow; [cf. नाडी-जङ्घ।]
नालिता: नालिता नालिता, f. an esculent root, Arum Colocasia.
नालीप: नालीप नालीप, अस्, m. = कदम्बक; per-haps for कडम्बक, the stalk of a pot-herb.
नालीव्रण: नालीव्रण नाली-व्रण, अस्, m. a fistulous or sinous sore (= नाडी-व्रण).
नाव: नाव 1. नाव, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 4. नु), Ved. a shout of joy or triumph.

नाव 2. नाव = 2. नौ, q. v., a boat, a ship, in Dvigu comps. after numerals and अर्ध (e. g. द्वि-नावम्, two boats; अर्ध-न्°, q. v., Pāṇ. V. 4, 99, 100). —नावाज (°व-अज), अस्, m., Ved. the steerer of a boat, a sailor. —नावोपजीवन (°व-उप्°), अस्, m. a sailor.
नाविक: नाविक, अस्, ई, अम्, belonging to a vessel, ship, boat, &c.; (अस्), m. (said to be fr. rt. नुद्), the helmsman of a vessel, the steersman, pilot; a pas-senger on board ship, a navigator, a sailor; (अम्), n., N. of a Sāman.
नाविन्: नाविन्, ई, m. a boatman, shipman, sailor.
नाव्य: 1. नाव्य, Nom. P. नाव्यति, &c., to wish for a ship.
2. नाव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, navigable; belonging to a boat; attainable or accessible by a boat or ship; (आ), f., Ved. a navigable river.
नाव्य 3. नाव्य, अम्, n. (fr. 1. नव), new-ness, novelty.
नावनीत: नावनीत नावनीत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. नव-नीत), mild.
नावमिक: नावमिक नावमिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. नवम), the ninth.
नावयज्ञिक: नावयज्ञिक नावयज्ञिक (fr. नव-यज्ञ), with काल, the time of offering the first-fruits &c. of the harvest.
नाश: नाश 1. नाश, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. नश्), Ved. attainment, obtaining; [cf. दू-णाश।]

नाश 2. नाश, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 2. नश्), dis-appearance; destruction, annihilation, ruin, loss; death; misfortune; abandonment, desertion; flight, retreat; (in arithmetic) elimination; [cf. कर्म-न्°, ग्रह-न्°, चित्त-न्°, दू-णाश।] —नाश-तस्, ind. = नाशात्, from death.
नाशक: नाशक, अस्, आ, अम्, destroying, destructive, anni-hilating, causing to perish; [cf. कु-न्°, कृत-न्°।]
नाशन: नाशन, अस्, ई, अम्, destroying, annihilating, causing to be lost, causing to perish, removing, (commonly in comp. with the object; cf. दुःस्वप्-न-न्°); (अम्), n. destruction, removing, removal, expulsion; ruin, perishing; forgetting.
नाशनीय: नाशनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, liable to be destroyed, destructible.
नाशयत्: नाशयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, destroying, annihilating, removing.
नाशयितृ: नाशयितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. a destroyer, remov-ing, a remover.
नाशित: नाशित, अस्, आ, अम्, destroyed, ruined, suffered to perish, lost.
नाशिन्: नाशिन्, ई, इनी, इ, destructive, destroying, a de-stroyer; removing; perishing, perishable, being lost or destroyed; [cf. अनर्थ-न्°, कुष्ठ-न्°, क्ष-य-न्°।]
नाशी: नाशी, f., N. of a river near Benares.
नाशुक: नाशुक, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. disappearing, perishing, being lost.
नाश्य: नाश्य, अस्, आ, अम्, liable to be destroyed, de-structible.
नाष्टिक: नाष्टिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. नष्ट), belonging or relating to anything lost; (अस्), m. the owner of anything lost, the former owner of a lost chattel.
नाष्ट्रा: नाष्ट्रा, f., Ved. danger, destruction; an evil spirit, a demon.
नास्: नास् 1. नास्, cl. 1. A. नासते, ननासे, नासितुम्, to sound.
नास् 2. नास्, Ved. the nose, in नासा, du. (Ṛg-veda II. 39, 6); [cf. 3. नस्।]
नासा: नासा, f. (said by some to be fr. rt. स्ना = rt. स्नु), the nose, (originally perhaps नासा, sing. = a nostril; नासे, du. = the two nostrils or the nose); a pro-boscis, the trunk of an elephant [cf. गज-न्°]; a piece of wood over a door projecting like a nose, the upper timber of a door [cf. नक्र]; the plant Gendarussa Vulgaris (= वासक); [cf. Lat. nāsus, nāris for nāsis; Old Germ. nāsa; Angl. Sax. nāse; Mod. Germ. nāse; Slav. nōsŭ; Lith. nōsis; Gr. νῆ-σος; Hib. neas, ‘a promontory,’ ness in Dunge-ness.] —नासाग्र (°सा-अग्°), अस्, m. the point or tip of the nose. —नासा-छिद्र, अम्, n. a nostril. —नासा-छिन्नी, f. a species of bird with a divided beak (= पूर्णिका). —नासा-ज्वर, अस्, m. a kind of disease of the nose (= नक्र). —नासा-दक्षिणावर्त (°ण-आव्°), अस्, m. wearing the nose-ring in the right nostril by rich women who have children (?). —नासा-दारु, n. = नासा, a piece of wood over a door pro-jecting like a nose; the upper timber of a door-frame. —नासा-नाह, अस्, m. thickening of the membrane of the nose, stoppage of the nostrils. —नासान्तिक, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. नासा-अन्त), reaching to the nose; [cf. केशान्तिक।] —नासा-परिशोष, अस्, m. heat and dryness of the nose. —नासा-परिस्राव, अस्, m. ‘nose-flow,’ running at the nose, a running cold. —नासा-पाक, अस्, m. a kind of disease of the nose attended with inflammation. —नासा-पुट, अस्, m. ‘nose-cup,’ the outside of the nostril, the nostril. —नासापुट-मर्यादा, f. the septum of the nose. —नासा-प्र-तीनाह, अस्, m. = नासा-नाह, thickening of the membrane of the nose, stoppage of the nostrils. —नासा-रक्त-पित्त, अम्, n. bleeding of the nose. —नासा-रन्ध्र, अम्, n. ‘nose-aperture,’ the nostril. —नासार्शस् (°सा-अर्°), आस्, m. polypus of the nose. —नासा-वंश, अस्, m. the bridge of the nose. —नासा-वामावर्त (°म-आव्°), अस्, m. wearing the nose-ring in the left nostril, a mark of sorrow or distress. —नासा-विवर, अस्, m. ‘nose-cavity,’ a nostril. —नासा-शोष, अस्, m. dryness of the nostrils. —नासा-संवेदन, अस्, m. Momordica Charantia (= काण्डीर-लता). —नासा-स्राव, अस्, m. = नासा-परिस्राव, ‘nose-flow,’ running at the nose, a running cold.
नासालु: नासालु, उस्, m. a tree, commonly Kāyaphal. See कट्फल, p. 196, col. 1.
नासिका: नासिका, f. the nose, (originally नासिका, sing. = a nostril; नासिके, du. = the two nostrils or the nose); the trunk of an elephant; a proboscis; any nose-shaped object [cf. चर्म-न्°]; a projection, the upper timber of a door; an epithet of the nymph Aśvinī; [cf. अ-नासिक, काक-नासिका, चर्म-न्°।] —नासिक-त्र्यम्बक-तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a sa-cred bathing-place mentioned in the Rasika-ramaṇa. —नासिकन्-धम, अस्, आ, अम् (नासिकम् for acc. sing. नासिकाम्), blowing or breathing through the nose, snoring, &c. —नासिकन्-धय, अस्, ई, अम् (नासिकम् for acc. sing. नासिकाम्), drinking through the nose. —नासिक-वत्, आन्, अती, अत् (for नासिका-वत्), Ved. having a nose. —नासिकाग्र (°क-अग्°), अम्, n. the tip of the nose. —नासिका-पाक, अस्, m. = नासा-पाक, a kind of disease or inflammation of the nose. —नासिका-पुट, अस्, m. = नासा-पुट, ‘nose-cup,’ the outside of the nostril, the nostril. —नासिका-मल, अम्, n. the mucus of the nose, snot.
नासिक्य: नासिक्य, अस्, आ, अम्, being in the nose; uttered through the nose, nasal; (अस्), m. any nasal sound; a peculiar nasal sound related to the so-called Yamas; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a people in Dakṣiṇā-patha; (औ), du. = नासत्यौ, the two sons of Aśvinī, the Aśvins; (अम्), n. the nose; N. of a town.
नास्य: नास्य, अम्, n. a nose-cord, the rein of a draught-ox passed through the septum of the nostrils; (perhaps collectively) noses, a multitude of noses (?); [cf. नस्य।]
नासत्य: नासत्य नासत्य, अस्, m. (derived by native commentators fr. न + अ-सत्य, ‘not untrue,’ or fr. नासा + affix त्य, or still more improbably fr. ना, nom. of नृ = नेतृ + सत्य), N. of one of the Aśvins, the other being then called Dasra; (औ), m. du. the common N. of the two Aśvins, see अश्विनौ; (आ), f. the constellation Aśvinī; (अस्, आ, अम्), re-ferring or relating to the Nāsatyas; [cf. Zend nā-onhaitya.]
नासमौजस: नासमौजस नासमौजस (न-अस्°), अस्, m., N. of the brother of Asamaujas and son of Kambala-barhiṣa.
नासीर: नासीर नासीर, अम्, n. advancing or skir-mishing in front of an army, leaving the line and defying or challenging the enemy by shouts and gestures; (अस्), m. the van or a champion who advances before the line; (also read नासिर।)
नास्ति: नास्ति नास्ति (न-अस्ति), ind. non-existence, not so, it is not. —नास्ति-ता, f. or नास्ति-त्व, अम्, n. non-existence. —नास्ति-वाद, अस्, m. “assertion of ‘it is not’ or of non-existence,” infidelity.
नास्तिक: नास्तिक, अस्, ई, अम्, atheistical, unbelieving, infidel, an unbeliever, applied by the orthodox Hindūs to any one who denies the divine authority of the Vedas and a future life, or doubts the legends of the Purāṇas; [cf. आस्तिक।] —नास्तिक-ता, f. or नास्तिक-त्व, अम्, n. or नास्तिक्य, अम्, n. infidelity, disbelief, atheism, denial of the deity, of a future state, of the authority of the Vedas, &c.; Buddhism, heresy, &c. —नास्तिक-मत, अम्, n. an atheistical opinion.
नास्तिद: नास्तिद नास्तिद or (according to others) नास्तितद, अस्, m. the mango tree (= आम्र).
नाह: नाह नाह, अस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. नह्), binding, confinement; a trap, a snare for catching deer &c.; obstruction in any organ or secretion of the body, as costiveness &c.
नाहल: नाहल नाहल, अस्, m. a man of a bar-barous or outcast tribe; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a non-Āryan people (= म्लेच्छ).
नाहुष: नाहुष 1. नाहुष, अस्, ई, अम्, (fr. नहुस्), Ved. neighbouring, being in the vicinity, neighbourly?; (Sāy.) human, belonging to men; (अस्), m. a neighbour.
नाहुष 2. नाहुष, अस्, m. (fr. नहुष), a patronymic of Yayāti; N. of a serpent-demon; [cf. नहुष।]
नाहुषि: नाहुषि, इस्, m. a patronymic of Yayāti.
नि: नि नि (an indeclinable prefix to verbs and nouns, used as a preposition except in one passage in Atharva-veda X. 8, 7, where it stands alone as an adverb), in, into, within; down, under, back; on, upon. As a prefix to nouns नि appears sometimes to be a curtailed form of निस् in its sense of ‘without,’ ‘deprived of’ (e. g. in नि-किल्विष, नि-खिल, q. v.), but the idea of negation in such compounds may pos-sibly be derived from the meanings ‘down,’ ‘down-wards,’ ‘back,’ which properly belong to नि; occasion-ally, however, नि is inaccurately written for निः (= निस्), as in नि-शब्द for निः-शब्द; according to native lexicographers the senses in which नि may be used are expressed by the following Sanskrit words, क्षेप, भृशार्थ, नित्यार्थ, दान, सन्-नि-धान, उप-रम, सं-श्रय, आ-श्रय, राशि, मोक्ष, अन्तर्-भाव, अधो-भाव, बन्धन, कौशल, नि-वेश, वि-न्य्-आस; [नि is thought by some to be for primitive अनि; cf. अन्-तर्, अन्-तरा; Gr. ἐν, ἐνί, εἰν, εἰς, ἐς for ἐν-ς, ἐν-τό-ς, ἔν-δο-ν, ἔσ-ω, ἔνεροι, ἔνερ-θε, ὑπ-ένερ-θε, ἐνέρ-τερο-ς, ἔντερο-ν; Lat. en-do, in-du, in, in-ter, in-trā, in-ter-ior, in-tumu-s, in-tus; Umbr. en, an-der; Osk. an-ter; Goth. in, inna, innuma, inna-thrō, un-dar; Mod. Germ. nieder; Angl. Sax. in, nidhan.]
निः निः, euphonically substituted for निस्, q. v., before श्, ष्, स्, and rarely before क्, ख्, प्, फ्।
निंस्: निंस् निंस् (thought by some to be a con-traction of निनंस्, old Desid. of rt. नम्), cl. 2. A. निंस्ते (2nd sing. निंस्से, 2nd sing. Impv. निंस्स्व), निनिंसे, निंसितुम्, &c., Ved. to touch, kiss, salute. (After प्र the initial न् is optionally cerebralized, cf. प्र-णिंसितव्य, प्र-निंसितव्य, परि-णिंसक; cf. also rt. निक्ष्।)
निः: निः निः, euphonically substituted for निस्, q. v., before श्, ष्, स्, and rarely before क्, ख्, प्, फ्।
निःक: निःक° निः-क°, निः-का°, &c. See under निष्-क°, निष्-का°, &c.
निःक्षत्र: निःक्षत्र निः-क्षत्र or निः-क्षत्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्, destitute of the military tribe, having no warrior-caste.
निःक्षिप्: निःक्षिप् निः-क्षिप्, probably for नि-क्षिप्, q. v.
निःक्षिप्त: निः-क्षिप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, thrown or sent away; spent (as time), passed.
निःक्षिप्य: निः-क्षिप्य, ind. having thrown or sent away; having spent (as time); having wiped away (as tears).
निःक्षेप: निः-क्षेप, अस्, m. throwing, sending, putting away; spending, passing (time); wiping away (as tears).
निःप: निःप° निः-प° and निः-फ°। See under निष्-प° and निष्-फ°।
निःशंसय: निःशंसय निः-शंसय, wrongly spelt for निः-संशय।
निःशङ्क: निःशङ्क निः-शङ्क, अस्, आ, अम्, free from fear, fearless, without misgiving or apprehension, having no cares, free from risk; (अम्), ind. fearlessly, without fear or care, without anxiety. —निःशङ्क-सुप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, sleeping without care, sleeping calmly and securely.
निःशङ्कित: निः-शङ्कित, अस्, आ, अम्, free from fear or care, free from risk, secure.
निःशब्द: निःशब्द निः-शब्द, अस्, आ, अम्, noiseless, soundless, not making a noise; (अस्, अम्), m. n. (?), soundlessness, silence, a calm; (अम्), ind. without noise, noiselessly; [cf. नि-शब्द।]
निःशम: निःशम निः-शम, अस्, m. uneasiness, dis-composure, anxiety.
निःशयान: निःशयान निः-शयान, अस्, आ, अम्, not sleep-ing, not lying down.
निःशरण: निःशरण निः-शरण, अस्, आ, अम्, without protection or refuge, defenceless, unprotected.
निःशर्कर: निःशर्कर निः-शर्कर, अस्, आ, अम्, free from stones or pebbles (as a bathing-place).
निःशलाक: निःशलाक निः-शलाक, अस्, आ, अम्, free from talking birds (as parrots, jays, or crows); solitary, private.
निःशल्य: निःशल्य निः-शल्य, अस्, आ, अम्, freed from an arrow; free from spikes or thorns; (अम्), ind. without an arrow; unthorny; without pain or diffi-culty; without reluctance, willingly.
निःशस्: निःशस् निः-शस्, f., Ved. refusing, declin-ing; (Sāy.) disinclination, absence of wish or desire, dislike (= निः-शंसन).
निःशस्त्र: निःशस्त्र निः-शस्त्र, अस्, आ, अम्, without arms, unarmed, weaponless.
निःशास्: निःशास् निः-शास् (निस्-श्°), cl. 2. P. -शास्ति, -शासितुम्, Ved. to order off or away; to expel.
निःशिष्: निःशिष् निः-शिष् (निस्-श्°), Caus. -शेषयति, -यितुम्, to take away or destroy completely, con-sume entirely, annihilate; (also regarded as a Nom. fr. निः-शेष।)
निःशेष: निः-शेष, अस्, आ, अम्, having no remainder, with-out remainder, completely spent, complete, entire, whole, (often in the sense of an adverb at the be-ginning of a comp. before a participle, e. g. निः-शेष-भग्न, completely broken); (अम् or एण), ind. completely, totally; निःशेषं कृ, to destroy or consume completely; [cf. अ-शेष।] —निःशेष-तस्, ind. without remainder, completely, totally. —निःशेष-ता, f. complete destruction.
निःशेषित: निः-शेषित, अस्, आ, अम्, having nothing left, com-pletely consumed or finished, destroyed, annihilated; (wrongly read नि-शेषित।)
निःशुक्र: निःशुक्र निः-शुक्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. without brilliancy; without virile energy, impotent.
निःशूक: निःशूक निः-शूक, अस्, m. beardless rice without any awn.
निःशोक: निःशोक निः-शोक, अस्, आ, अम्, free from sorrow or care.
निःशोध्य: निःशोध्य निः-शोध्य, अस्, आ, अम्, not to be purified, not requiring cleansing; clean, pure.
निःश्मश्रु: निःश्मश्रु निः-श्मश्रु, उस्, उस्, उ, beardless; (wrongly read नि-श्मश्रु।)
निःश्रयणी: निःश्रयणी निः-श्रयणी or निः-श्रयिणी, f. a ladder, a staircase, steps, &c.; [cf. नि-श्रयणी, नि-श्रयिणी।]
निःश्रेणि: निः-श्रेणि, इस्, ई, f. a ladder or staircase, a flight of stairs or steps; the wild date tree.
निःश्रेणिका: निःश्रेणिका, f. a species of grass.
निःश्री: निःश्री निः-श्री, ईस्, ईस्, इ, deprived of happi-ness or prosperity, unfortunate. —निःश्री-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made unfortunate, rendered unhappy.
निःश्रीक: निःश्रीक, अस्, आ, अम्, deprived of beauty (as a dead body), deprived of happiness, &c.; one whose happiness is destroyed, unhappy, inglorious; (also read नि-श्रीक।) —निःश्रीक-ता, f. absence of good fortune, want of good luck.
निःश्रेयस: निःश्रेयस निः-श्रेयस, अस्, ई, अम्, having nothing better or superior, the best, most excellent; (अस्), m. an epithet of Śiva; (अम्), n. final beatitude, ultimate bliss or supreme felicity in the life to come, happiness, welfare; knowledge which brings deliver-ance, learning; belief, faith, devotedness; appre-hension, conception.
निःश्वस्: निःश्वस् निः-श्वस्, cl. 2. P. -श्वसिति, -श्वसि-तुम्, to breathe out, expire, sigh.
निःश्वसन: निः-श्वसन, अम्, n. breathing out, sighing.
निःश्वसित: निः-श्वसित, अस्, आ, अम्, breathed out, sighed; sighing, breathing out; (अम्), n. sighing, expiration, a sigh.
निःश्वस्य: निः-श्वस्य, ind. having sighed, sighing, breath-ing out.
निःश्वास: निः-श्वास, अस्, m. breathing out, expiration; breath, sighing, a sigh; (often read नि-श्वास।) —निः-श्वास-परम, अस्, आ, अम्, chiefly engaged in sigh-ing, melancholy, sorrowful. —निःश्वास-संहिता, f., N. of a code of laws supposed to have been revealed by Rudra-Śiva.
निःषमम्: निःषमम् निः-षमम्, ind. (fr. निस् + स-मम्), at the wrong time, unseasonably.
निःषिध्: निःषिध् निः-षिध्, त्, f. (fr. निस् + सिध् = साध्), granting, bestowing; grant, oblation, gift, donation; (Sāy.) hindrance, obstruction; destroying, destructive, adverse.
निःषिध्वन्: निः-षिध्वन्, आ, अरी, अ (fr. निस् + सिध्वन्), Ved. granting, presenting; (Sāy.) coming to com-plete perfection.
निःसंशय: निःसंशय निः-संशय, अस्, आ, अम्, un-doubted, infallible, unerring, certain; not doubting, not doubtful; (अम्), ind. without doubt, doubtless, infallibly, certainly, surely.
निःसङ्कक्ष: निःसङ्कक्ष निः-सङ्कक्ष, अस्, आ, अम्, not per-plexed, not confused; (also written नि-सङ्कक्ष।)
निःसङ्ख्य: निःसङ्ख्य निः-सङ्ख्य, अस्, आ, अम्, innu-merable, numberless.
निःसङ्ग: निःसङ्ग निः-सङ्ग, अस्, आ, अम्, unattached, unobstructed; not attached, not devoted, regardless, indifferent to (with loc.); free from worldly attach-ment or selfish desires, unselfish, disinterested; un-connected, separated; (एन or अम्), ind. without attachment, without interest, unselfishly, without further reflection; (also written निः-षङ्ग; cf. अ-सङ्ग।) —निःसङ्ग-ता, f. or निःसङ्ग-त्व, अम्, n. absence of attachment, unselfishness, disinterested-ness, indifference.
निःसञ्चार: निःसञ्चार निः-सञ्चार, अस्, आ, अम्, not mov-ing, not walking about, not leaving one's home.
निःसञ्ज्ञ: निःसञ्ज्ञ निः-सञ्ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्, senseless, insensible, unconscious.
निःसत्त्व: निःसत्त्व निः-सत्त्व, अस्, आ, अम्, without courage or strength, unenergetic, weak, impotent; insignificant, low, mean; non-existent, unsubstantial; deprived of living beings; (अम्), n. absence of power, want of energy; insignificance; non-existence.
निःसत्य: निःसत्य निः-सत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, untrue, false. —निःसत्य-ता, f. insincerity, falsehood, untruth.
निःसन्तति: निःसन्तति निः-सन्तति, इस्, इस्, इ, destitute of offspring, childless.
निःसन्तान: निः-सन्तान, अस्, आ, अम्, destitute of posterity, childless.
निःसन्दिग्ध: निःसन्दिग्ध निः-सन्दिग्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, un-doubted, not doubtful, certain; (अम्), ind. without any doubt, certainly.
निःसन्देह: निः-सन्देह, अस्, आ, अम्, free from uncertainty, doubtless, undoubted, certain; (अम्), ind. without any doubt, certainly.
निःसन्धि: निःसन्धि निः-सन्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, having no joints, having no joints perceptible, well knit, com-pact, close, firm.
निःसपत्न: निःसपत्न निः-सपत्न, अस्, आ, अम्, having no rival, not sharing the possession of anything with another; not claimed by another, belonging exclu-sively to one possessor; having no enemies.
निःसम्पात: निःसम्पात निः-सम्पात, अस्, आ, अम्, afford-ing no passage, blocked up; (अस्), m. thick dark-ness, midnight.
निःसम्बन्ध: निःसम्बन्ध निः-सम्बन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, with-out relatives.
निःसम्बाध: निःसम्बाध निः-सम्बाध, अस्, आ, अम्, not contracted, large, spacious.
निःसम्भ्रम: निःसम्भ्रम निः-सम्भ्रम, अस्, आ, अम्, not perplexed or flurried, unembarrassed.
निःसरण: निःसरण निः-सरण। See under निः-सृ, col. 2.

निः-सरण, अम्, n. going forth or out, coming forth, exit; the egress or outlet from a house, market-place, town, &c., the gate, the gate-way; a means or expedient, a remedy; departure, dying, death; final beatitude.
निःसलिल: निःसलिल निः-सलिल, अस्, आ, अम्, waterless, having no water.
निःसह: निःसह निः-सह, अस्, आ, अम्, unable to bear or support or resist, impatient; powerless, weak; intolerable, unbearable, irresistible. —निःसह-ता, f. or निःसह-त्व, अम्, n. inability to bear or support; impatience, unendurance.
निःसहाय: निःसहाय निः-सहाय, अस्, आ, अम्, without helpers or associates, unassisted.
निःसाध्वस: निःसाध्वस निः-साध्वस, अस्, आ, अम्, fearless, bold; (अम्), ind. fearlessly, boldly. —निःसाध्वस-त्व, अम्, n. fearlessness, boldness.
निःसामर्थ्य: निःसामर्थ्य निः-सामर्थ्य, अस्, आ, अम्, unfit, unsuitable.
निःसामान्य: निःसामान्य निः-सामान्य, अस्, आ, अम्, extra-ordinary, uncommon, unusual, special.
निःसार: निःसार 1. निः-सार, अस्, आ, अम् (for 2. निः-सार see under निः-सृ below), sapless, pithless, worthless, vain, vapid, unsubstantial; (अस्), m. the plant Trophis Aspera; a kind of time in music; (आ), f. the pisang, Musa Sapientum (= कदली). —निःसार-ता, f. saplessness, worthlessness, vanity.
2. निः-सार, अस्, m. (for 1. निः-सार see above), going forth or out.
निःसाल: निःसाल निः-साल, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. being out of the house.
निःसीमन्: निःसीमन् निः-सीमन्, आ, आ, अ, immeasurable, having no boundaries or limits.
निःसुख: निःसुख निः-सुख, अस्, आ, अम्, joyless, sad, unhappy; disagreeable, distressing.
निःसृ: निःसृ निः-सृ (निस्-स्°), cl. 1. P. -सरति, -सर्तुम्, to go out, come forth, issue, slip out, depart, withdraw: Caus. -सारयति, -यितुम्, to cause to go out or away, turn out, expel.
निःसर: निः-सर, अस्, आ, अम्, issuing out. —निःसर-त्व, अम्, n. = पित्त-रोग।
निःसारण: निः-सारण, अम्, n. driving out, expelling, turn-ing out; the egress or outlet from a building, town, &c., a passage, road of ingress or egress.
निःसारित: निः-सारित, अस्, आ, अम्, turned out, made to come out, expelled, dismissed.
निःसार्य: निः-सार्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be turned out, to be excluded or expelled.
निःसृत: निः-सृत, अस्, आ, अम्, gone forth or out, broken forth; having departed (with abl.).
निःस्तम्भ: निःस्तम्भ निः-स्तम्भ, अस्, आ, अम्, without posts or columns, having no pillars.
निःस्तुति: निःस्तुति निः-स्तुति, इस्, इस्, इ (also read नि-स्तुति), praising nothing, without praising (anything).
निःस्नेह: निःस्नेह निः-स्नेह, अस्, आ, अम्, without unction, not greasy or unctuous, dry; without love or affection, insensible, cold, unfeeling; not longing for, indifferent; not loved, uncared for, hated; (आ), f. linseed, Linum Usitatissimum. —निःस्नेह-फला, f. a species of Solanum with white flowers.
निःस्पन्द: निःस्पन्द निः-स्पन्द, अस्, आ, अम्, motionless.
निःस्पृह: निःस्पृह निः-स्पृह, अस्, आ, अम् (often written नि-स्पृह), free from desire; disregarding, indiffer-ent to (with abl.); content, unenvious.
निःस्रु: निःस्रु निः-स्रु (निस्-स्°), Caus. -स्रावयति, -यितुम्, to cause to flow out or off, to empty.
निःस्रव: निः-स्रव, अस्, m. remainder, surplus, overplus (with abl.).
निःस्राव: निः-स्राव, अस्, m. causing to flow out, expending, expense; the moisture or water of boiled rice; [cf. नि-स्राव।]
निःस्व: निःस्व निः-स्व, अस्, आ, अम्, deprived of one's own, having no property, indigent, poor. —निःस्व-ता, f. poverty. —निःस्वी-कृत or निःस्वी-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, deprived of one's property, impoverished.
